    Important Words
    • īśitavyatām — the status of being controlled
      Abstract noun from īśitavya (to be controlled). The very condition Bhagavān is pretending to be in. Gauḍīyas read this as the philosophical heart of Kṛṣṇa's nara-līlā: He plays the īśitavya so the īśvaras of His creation may serve Him without distance.
    • jana-saṅgrahaḥ — the enlightenment of the people
      jana (people) + saṅgraha (gathering, taking care of). The same phrase Kṛṣṇa Himself uses at BG 3.20, 3.25 — loka-saṅgrahaḥ. Gauḍīyas note the structural reciprocity: He acts for jana-saṅgraha; His devotee acts likewise.
    • smayantaḥ — smiling
      From √smi (to smile). The smile is the diagnostic that the sages have understood. Gauḍīyas treat the smile of a Vaiṣṇava sage as a small mudrā — interior recognition surfacing on the face.
    • jagat-gurum — the spiritual master of the universe
      jagat (world) + guru (heavy, weighty, teacher). Kṛṣṇa is the original ādi-guru. The sages address Him so even as He pretends subordination — the smile says, we know who is teaching whom.
    For some time the sages pondered the Supreme Lord’s behavior, which resembled that of a subordinate living being. They concluded that He was acting this way to instruct the people in general. Thus they smiled and spoke to Him, the spiritual master of the universe.
    Purport

    Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī explains the word īśitavyatā as referring to one’s not being a controller, or in other words, to being under the law of karma, obliged to work and experience the results of one’s work. While addressing the sages, Lord Kṛṣṇa accepted the role of a subordinate living being to emphasize the importance of hearing and serving saintly Vaiṣṇavas. The Personality of Godhead is also the supreme teacher of spiritual surrender.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    For some time the sages pondered the Supreme Lord's behavior, which resembled that of a subordinate living being. They concluded that He was acting this way to instruct the people in general. Thus they smiled and spoke to Him, the spiritual master of the universe.
    Commentary

    After considering the Lord’s statement that He was subservient to them (isvarasya isitavyatam), they could not see any logic in his statements. Therefore they explained that his words and actions were for teaching the common man (jana sangraha) by the Lord who establishes dharma, because he is the teacher of the universe (jagat gurum).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    They considered for a long time why he was acting as if controlled and concluded that he must be acting with humility according to his human pastimes, as he had the best qualities, since he did not lack power , had no desire for power and did not lack knowledge. Looking at each other with astonishment, shyness and bliss, they smiled. He acted in this way in order to teach the people, or to attract the devotees (jana-saṅgraḥ) since he was the originator of all good qualities (jagad-guruḥ).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    They considered a long time the Lord’s acting as a controlled being and smiled at his use of words, after they understood. It was for instructing the people, since he was guru of the universe. They then spoke to him. Or considering his acting as a jīva was to teach people, understanding the meaning of his words, or by his humble behavior, as the ocean of good qualities, they slightly smiled with devotion, since it would be improper to laught out loud. They then spoke to him, in the following verses.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A wrestling master, sparring with students, will sometimes fall to the floor on purpose so the lesson lands. Kṛṣṇa playing the subordinate in the assembly is the same: jana-saṅgraha — gathering the people — is a teaching technique, and the smile of the sages who recognize it is the smile of advanced students seeing through the master's deliberate stumble.

    Stories
    Kṛṣṇa as Arjuna's charioteer

    Throughout the Mahābhārata, Bhagavān takes the lower seat — Arjuna's sārathi — though He is sarva-loka-maheśvara (BG 5.29). The sages here recognize at Kurukṣetra the same pattern they had seen earlier on the same field eighteen years before.

    Gauḍīyas hold this as Kṛṣṇa's signature: the highest authority adopts the lower form so His devotees can serve without intimidation.

    Important Words
    • tattva-vit — knower of the truth
      tattva (truth, that-ness) + vit (knower). The technical Sanskrit philosopher's title. The sages claim it and immediately disclaim it under Bhagavān's māyā. Gauḍīyas read this as the necessary humility of any philosopher in front of Kṛṣṇa.
    • māyayā — by Your māyā
      Bhagavān's power of bewilderment. Gauḍīyas distinguish yoga-māyā (internal, hides Kṛṣṇa's aiśvarya from devotees so rasa may flow) from mahā-māyā (external, hides Him from non-devotees). The next verses make clear this is yoga-māyā.
    • viśva-sṛjām — of the creators of the universe
      viśva + sṛj (to emit, create). The Prajāpatis and co-creators headed by Brahmā. The sages are calling themselves the cosmic CEOs — and saying even we are confused. Gauḍīyas note the rhetorical pressure: if these are confused, what of an ordinary watcher?
    • viceṣṭitam — the activity
      vi + √ceṣṭ (to move, act). Bhagavān's līlā is viceṣṭita — extraordinary action. Gauḍīyas hold that līlā is the proper category, not karma: action without bondage, performed for rasa, not phala.
    The great sages said: Your power of illusion has totally bewildered us, the most exalted knowers of the truth and leaders among the universal creators. Ah, how amazing is the behavior of the Supreme Lord! He covers Himself with His humanlike activities and pretends to be subject to superior control.
    Purport

    The sages have characterized the Lord’s statements as inscrutable ( duranvayam ). How this is so is stated here: His words and activities bewilder even the most learned when He plays at subordinating Himself to His own servants.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The great sages said: Your power of illusion has totally bewildered us, the most exalted knowers of the truth and leaders among the universal creators. Ah, how amazing is the behavior of the Supreme Lord! He covers Himself with His humanlike activities and pretends to be subject to superior control.
    Commentary

    Though you are the supreme lord, you are bhagavan, who acts as if you were a controlled jiva, being difficult to perceive (gudha) because of your human activities (ihaya). But these actions produce your fame (bhagavat vicestitam). According to the amara kosa bhaga means wealth, desire, glory, courage, effort the sun and fame.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Again it is said that they spoke (munayaḥ ucuḥ). Five verses describe their words. Two verses explain how his words were incoherent. We are bewildered by his inconceivable śakti (māyayā), his activities (viceṣṭitam), even though we know all about how he takes various forms (tattva-vid-uttamāḥ). You hide yourself by your human actions and act as if you were not the Lord. Or, though he is difficult to understand through the Vedas, the Lord acts like a jīva in his various pastimes (ihayā). Parasmaipada verb form of īśitavyāyati is poetic license.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    They speak in five verses. How amazing are activities of the Lord. By his (yat) māyā, we, Brahmā and others, lords of prajāpatis like Marīci (viśva-sṛjām), are bewildered even more than their subjects since they think they are great knowers of the truth. Or because they are bewildered the controllers of creators of the universe think themselves great Prajāpatis. How amazing (aho)! Though not understood easily by the Vedas you act like a jīva (īśatavyāyati), with various pastimes (īhayā). Or covered by many matters, acting like a jīva by your māyā, people are bewildered. “Why do cover you with māyā?” Oh (aho)! They lament and recite the verse.

    • Bhanu Sw SB 10-84-16 - Krishna%27s pastimes are bewildering even to great Personalities - 2008-04-08
      His Holiness Bhanu Swami· 2008-04-08· English
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    An astronomer measures the orbits of planets, then steps out at dusk and forgets to look up. The sages confess: we have been the cataloguers of the truth and yet Your māyā has confused us, the very ones who name the categories. Kṛṣṇa as nara-līlā is the planet we keep failing to lift our eyes to.

    Stories
    Brahmā stealing the calves

    Brahmā, the chief sṛjāṁ adhīśvara, in SB 10.13 actively tests Kṛṣṇa — and is undone. He says afterward, naumīḍya te 'bhra-vapuṣe — I bow to You whose form is like a cloud (10.14.1), praising the very līlā he had doubted.

    Gauḍīyas pair this confession with the present one: knowers of the truth, when confronted with Bhagavān's nara-līlā, become the first to confess bewilderment.

    📝 My note

    Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.84.17

    Important Words
    • anīhaḥ — exerting no endeavor
      a- (not) + īhā (effort). Bhagavān creates without straining. Gauḍīyas read this as a marker of His aiśvarya: His will is enacted directly, without the labor that conditioned beings require to produce anything.
    • ekaḥ — alone, one
      Bhagavān creates alone — without a second agent. Personalist reading: not impersonal oneness, but one Person acting from His own Self. Gauḍīyas insist that the One here is Kṛṣṇa as svayaṁ-bhagavān, not a featureless Brahman.
    • bhaumaiḥ — by the transformations of earth
      From bhūmi (earth). The pots, pillars, idols. The famous Upaniṣadic analogy compressed into one ablative. Gauḍīyas use it to show that the world's variety is not an illusion — it is a transformation of the substrate, distinguishable from but not separable from the substrate.
    • viḍambanam — a pretense, mimicry
      From vi + √ḍamb (to mock, mimic). Bhagavān's humanlike activity is viḍambana — He plays at being conditioned. Gauḍīyas treat this as the doctrinal description of nara-līlā: the form is imitative; the Person within is unaffected.
    Indeed, the humanlike pastimes of the Almighty are simply a pretense! Effortlessly, He alone sends forth from His Self this variegated creation, maintains it and then swallows it up again, all without becoming entangled, just as the element earth takes on many names and forms in its various transformations.
    Purport

    The one Supreme expands Himself as many without diminishing His completeness. He does this effortlessly, without depending on anyone or anything else. This mystic process of the Lord’s self-expansion is incomprehensible to all but Himself, but the example of the substance earth and its manifold products bears enough resemblance to provide some idea. The same example is also presented in an often-cited passage of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (6.1), vācārambhaṇaṁ vikāro nāmadheyaṁ mṛttikety eva satyam: “Earth’s transformations are merely verbal creations of the process of naming; the substance earth itself is alone real.” Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī suggests that this verse of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam answers a possible objection on the part of Lord Kṛṣṇa: “How can I create, maintain and destroy the universe if I am Vasudeva’s son?” The answer is given by the words aho vibhūmnaś caritaṁ viḍambanam: “You are the perfectly complete whole, and Your birth and pastimes are only an imitation of ordinary persons’ activities in the material world. You simply pretend to be under higher control.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Indeed, the humanlike pastimes of the Almighty are simply a pretense! Effortlessly, He alone sends forth from His Self this variegated creation, maintains it and then swallows it up again, all without becoming entangled, just as the element earth takes on many names and forms in its various transformations.
    Commentary

    Both show of power and hiding your powers are beyond comprehension. The Lord creates this universe (etat) by himself (atmana) with many forms, but is not bound. Though the lord is one (ekah) he becomes the universe with many names and forms, just as earth is one, but becomes many as a pot or cloth. Amazing (aho) are the actions of the completely perfect lord (vibhumnah), appearing to be a controlled jiva by worshipping the sages. But it is only a pretense of being a controlled jiva (vidambanam).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    This happens all the time, not just now. You are one, without assistance. By yourself, without the assistance of another cause, by your svarūpa, you create and destroy even the whole universe, but you are without change (anīhaḥ) by action or by transformation. There is great variety (bahudhā) by manifestation of many different universes and various times. You are complete in yourself (vibhumnaḥ). Therefore your actions mock our intelligence (viḍambanam), since you possess acintya-śakti. Śrutes tu śabda-mūlatvāt: contradictions in the Lord are explained by scripture alone. (Brahma-sūtra 2.1.27)

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The Lord is without action (anīhaḥ), unlike the potter in making the pot. Just by his desire things are accomplished. Or he has not purpose in creating the variegated universe (anīhaḥ). Alone you create by yourself (ātmanā). You are not dependent on anyone else. But you are not bound up by karma. It is just like (yathā) earth manifesting many names and forms with transformations. Aho indicates joy. The actions of the complete Lord (vibhūmnaḥ) are a pretense. “If he is complete why does he flee from Jarāsandha?” That is the pretense. By such activities he deceives the demons. Or the Lord is not at all bound up (yathā) because (hi) even earth with its names and forms is not bound by its products (bhaumaiḥ). It is not transformed. “What is the purpose in my creating the universe?” It is for the benefit of the jīvas. The activities of creation and destruction (caritam) are for supporting (vilambanam) all the jīvas. The letter L can be substituted for Ḍ.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The element earth, going about its single business of being earth, becomes a pot, a pillar, a wall, a road, a Deity, a corpse, without ceasing to be earth. So Bhagavān, in His ekatva, sends forth the variegated worlds and reabsorbs them without being snagged by any of it. The pot does not entangle the clay.

    Stories
    Chāndogya Upaniṣad's earthen pot

    The Chāndogya (6.1.4) uses the same image — yathā saumya ekena mṛt-piṇḍena sarvaṁ mṛn-mayaṁ vijñātaṁ syāt — by knowing one lump of clay, all earthen things are known.

    Gauḍīyas read the Upaniṣad's image through acintya-bhedābheda: the names and forms are real (not māyā in the Advaitin sense), and yet the substratum is one Person. The verse here applies that image to Bhagavān's līlā.

    Important Words
    • sattvam — the mode of goodness
      Here, Gauḍīyas read this as śuddha-sattva, not the material guṇa. Jīva Gosvāmī (Bhāgavata-sandarbha) distinguishes Bhagavān's form as constituted of viśuddha-sattva — the unmixed mode, the substance of His descents.
    • veda-patham — the path of the Vedas
      veda + patha (path). The Vedic dharma-mārga that culminates in Kṛṣṇa-bhakti (SB 1.2.6). Gauḍīyas hold that protecting veda-patha is the same as protecting bhakti — the two are continuous, not rivals.
    • sanātanam — eternal
      The Veda's path is not historical; it is eternal. Gauḍīyas use sanātana as a technical term for the eternal nature of dharma (sanātana-dharma) and of one's relationship with Bhagavān (sanātana-yoga, BG 4.3).
    • varṇa-āśrama-ātmā — the Soul of the varṇāśrama order
      varṇa (social order) + āśrama (life-stage) + ātmā (Self). Bhagavān is the inner Person of the varṇāśrama structure. Gauḍīyas note this as the reason varṇāśrama is not optional pluralism — it is Kṛṣṇa's own social body, designed to converge on bhakti.
    Nonetheless, at suitable times You assume the pure mode of goodness to protect Your devotees and punish the wicked. Thus You, the Soul of the varṇāśrama social order, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, maintain the eternal path of the Vedas by enjoying Your pleasure pastimes.
    Purport

    This verse describes the Lord’s enlightening people in general ( jana-saṅgraha ) and His imitation of worldly behavior. Because the Personality of Godhead remains always perfect, the body He manifests when He comes to this world is not touched by material goodness; rather, it is a manifestation of the pure goodness known as viśuddha-sattva, the same spiritual substance that constitutes His original form.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Nonetheless, at suitable times You assume the pure mode of goodness to protect Your devotees and punish the wicked. Thus You, the Soul of the varṇāśrama social order, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, maintain the eternal path of the Vedas by enjoying Your pleasure pastimes.
    Commentary

    You put on this pretense in order to protect the devotees, destroy the demons and establish dharma. This is explained in three verses. Being the supreme, perfect lord, you accept a suddha sattva form (sattvam vibharsi) (to protect the devotees and destroy the demons), and by your conduct (svalilaya) accept the eternal path of the Vedas. Because of this, you institute the varnas and asramas (varnasrama atma). But still you remain the supreme among all the different forms that you manifest as mentioned above (purusah parah).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though you have inconceivable śakti, at some time you clearly support sattva to protect your devotees and punish the wicked. In doing that as your pastime, you institute varṇāśrama and you nourish the path of the eternal Vedas. This is incomprehensible to us. How can we understand you? You surpass all methods of intelligence (paraḥ).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though you support rajas for creation, at the time of maintenance (kale) you support or protect sattva, to protect (guptaye) your devotees (sva) by promiting real dharma (abhi) and punish the demons by killing them. You nourish the eternal path of the Vedas- which are your form. vedo nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣāt: the Vedas are directly Nārāyaṇa and are born from him. (SB 6.1.40) Or you nourish the path of the Vedas, which always exists. Thus it must always be protected. Or you nourish the path of the Vedas, which spreads (atanam), giving of the highest benefit (san). You do this by spreading varṇāśrama, because you are the supreme Lord (paraḥ puruṣaḥ). You are the protector internally as antaryāmī, similulator of the senses, and externally as various avatāras, by destroying the obstacles created by non-believers. This is for the benefit of all jīvas. Or thus, at the appropriate time, you support the sattvic heart or you support existence (sattvam). This means you become visible to protect the devotees and punish the demons. Thus you support the path of the Vedas.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A king walks the streets in plain clothes for half the year, but on coronation day puts on the regalia so that justice may be visibly enacted. Kṛṣṇa wears the pure mode of sattva as that regalia: nara-līlā in plain dress, descent in śuddha-sattva for the explicit act of protection and chastisement.

    Stories
    Nṛsiṁha descending for Prahlāda

    In SB 7.8, Bhagavān manifests as Nṛsiṁhadeva at the precise moment Prahlāda needs protection — śuddha-sattva personified as half-man, half-lion, killing Hiraṇyakaśipu in the doorway.

    Gauḍīyas hold Nṛsiṁha-līlā as the paradigm of sva-jana-abhiguptaye — protection of the devotee — referenced in this verse.

    Important Words
    • brahma — the Vedas
      Here brahma = the Vedas, śabda-brahman. Gauḍīyas distinguish three referents of brahma — śabda-brahman (the scriptures), nirviśeṣa-brahman (the impersonal effulgence), and svayaṁ-bhagavān (the Person, of whom brahman is the bodily glow, BG 14.27). The verse here means the first.
    • hṛdayam — heart
      The Vedas are not Bhagavān's calling card; they are His hṛdaya. Gauḍīyas read this as the warrant for treating the Bhāgavatam (called nigamasya kalpa-taroḥ galitam phalam, SB 1.1.3) as Kṛṣṇa-vāṇī — His heart speaking.
    • śuklam — pure, spotless
      From √śuc (to shine, be pure). The Veda is uncontaminated revelation. Gauḍīyas insist on the Veda's apauruṣeyatva — not human-authored — which is why śuklam is grammatically possible.
    • tapaḥ-svādhyāya-saṁyamaiḥ — by austerity, study, and self-control
      The classical brāhmaṇa-triad. Gauḍīyas note that bhakti subsumes all three: tapas as voluntary restraint for sevā, svādhyāya as hearing kṛṣṇa-kathā, saṁyama as senses turned toward Bhagavān (hṛṣīkeṇa-hṛṣīkeśa-sevanam, Padma Purāṇa).
    • param — transcendental, supreme
      The Vedas reveal vyakta, avyakta, and tataḥ param — what is beyond both. Gauḍīyas read param as Bhagavān Himself: the Veda points past manifest and unmanifest to the akṣara puruṣottama (BG 15.18).
    The Vedas are Your spotless heart, and through them one can perceive — by means of austerity, study and self-control — the manifest, the unmanifest and the pure existence transcendental to both.
    Purport

    Vyakta, “the manifest,” consists of the visible things of this world, and avyakta consists of the subtle, underlying causes of cosmic creation. The Vedas point toward the transcendental realm of Brahman, which lies beyond all material cause and effect.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Vedas are Your spotless heart, and through them one can perceive—by means of austerity, study and self-control—the manifest, the unmanifest and the pure existence transcendental to both.
    Commentary

    You follow the path of the Vedas, because the Vedas are very dear to you (the statement is mentioned in the previous verse). The pure (suklam) Vedas (brahma) are your heart in which cause (avyaktam) and effect (vyaktam) and existence itself, Brahman (param), are realized through austerity study and sense control.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “Do you protect your devotees by nourishing the path of the Vedas?” The Vedas (brahma) are your form (hṛdayam) made of pure mercy (śuklam). In the Vedas, by performing all rites, by learning all its meanings, by controlling the mind from wandering elsewhere, the supreme Brahman, Bhagavān (paraḥ), beyond the visible universe (vyaktam) and prakṛti (avyaktam) is realized. By supporting the Vedas you support your devotees.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having shown the eternal nature of the Vedas, the cause for respecting the brāhmaṇas is explained in two verses. In the Vedas the devotees can understand the supreme lord and prakṛti by follow sva-dharma, study of the Vedas, and performance of vratas. Though study is included in following sva-dharma it is mentioned separately in this case because of its great importance. Or by the Vedas Svarga (vyaktam) and impersonal Brahman (avyaktam), and then what is most excellent, bhakti, is realized. In the Vedas (yatra) this is attained (upalabdham). This means by the Vedas, this is attained. Or brahman can mean the brāhmaṇas. By them one can attain realization of bhakti etc.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The Vedas are Kṛṣṇa's spotless heart — the one place where what He is can be exactly traced. Through tapas, svādhyāya, and saṁyama, the disciple presses an ear to that heart and hears, in sequence, the manifest world (vyakta), the unmanifest cause (avyakta), and the pure Person beyond both. The textbook is a stethoscope, not a wall.

    Stories
    Śuka receiving the Bhāgavatam

    Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who narrates this whole work, internalized the Bhāgavatam from his father Vyāsa through exactly the triad named here — tapas, svādhyāya, saṁyama (SB 1.4–7).

    Gauḍīyas treat Śuka's reception of the text as the working example of the verse: the Veda accessed through proper discipline reveals not abstractions but Kṛṣṇa.

    Important Words
    • brahmaṇya — of those who respect brahminical culture
      From brāhmaṇa + -ya (relating to). Kṛṣṇa is brahmaṇya-deva — the God who honors brāhmaṇas (SB 10.84.20, Viṣṇu-sahasra-nāma names Him brahmaṇyaḥ). Gauḍīyas insist this title names Him before any of the sovereign epithets — He is first the friend of brāhmaṇas, then king.
    • agranīḥ — the foremost, leader
      agra (front) + nī (leading). Kṛṣṇa is the agranīḥ — the leader — of brāhmaṇa-respecters. Gauḍīyas note that the model He sets becomes the binding standard: a Vaiṣṇava cannot ignore brāhmaṇa-pūjā if Bhagavān Himself enacts it.
    • śāstra-yoneḥ — whose means of realization is śāstra
      śāstra + yoni (source, womb). The brāhmaṇas are the womb through which śāstra becomes realizable. Gauḍīyas read this as the rationale for guru-paramparā: the text alone does not transmit; the brāhmaṇa-vaiṣṇava transmits.
    • sat-dhāma — the perfect abode
      sat (true, existent) + dhāma (abode). The brāhmaṇa-kula is called the abode of sat. Gauḍīyas distinguish this from the brāhmaṇa-by-birth: the verse intends those whose conduct manifests sat — that is, the Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa.
    Therefore, O Supreme Brahman, You honor the members of the brahminical community, for they are the perfect agents by which one can realize You through the evidence of the Vedas. For that very reason You are the foremost worshiper of the brāhmaṇas.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Therefore, O Supreme Brahman, You honor the members of the brahminical community, for they are the perfect agents by which one can realize You through the evidence of the Vedas. For that very reason You are the foremost worshiper of the brāhmaṇas.
    Commentary

    You worship the brahmanas who are the best source of realization (sad dhama) of yourself (atmanah) who is proven by the Veda (sastra yoneh).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “If I am like that, why do I worship you sages?” You honor the brāhmaṇas to teach the people. In the manner that they started the discussion with this concept, they finish with the same statement.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    You worship the brāhmaṇas, for they are your (ātmanaḥ) excellent (sat) abode (dhāma), since you are the promoter of the Vedas (śāstra-yoneḥ). O direct form of the Vedas (brahman)! The brāhmaṇas are the abode of the Lord because they possess or promote the Vedas. Thus it is proper that the Lord worships them.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Kṛṣṇa as brahmaṇya-deva is the king who calls his prime minister 'my elder' in public, not because the minister outranks him but because the office of brāhmaṇa is the channel by which the kingdom recognizes its sovereign. Bhagavān honors the brāhmaṇa because that is how He chooses to be honored.

    Stories
    Kṛṣṇa serving Sudāmā

    Again the Sudāmā episode (SB 10.80–81): the Lord, who owns all opulences, washes the feet of a brāhmaṇa friend whose only wealth is his loyalty to vidyā and his memory of guru-kula.

    Gauḍīyas hold that scene as the lived form of this verse — brahmaṇya-deva in action, not merely in epithet.

    Caitanya at Advaita Ācārya's house

    Mahāprabhu, the same Bhagavān incarnate in Gauḍa-deśa, repeatedly took the lower position in Advaita Ācārya's house. Caitanya-caritāmṛta records Advaita scolding Him for it; He kept doing it.

    Gauḍīyas read this as proof that brahmaṇya behavior is not period-specific — Bhagavān honors the brāhmaṇa-Vaiṣṇava in every age.

    Important Words
    • sat-gatyā — the goal of saintly persons
      sat (true) + gati (goal). Kṛṣṇa is what sat-persons are heading toward. Gauḍīyas hold the prayojana of all the regulative limbs (sambandha-abhidheya) to be kṛṣṇa-prema, which is what 'sat-gati' here ultimately names.
    • sāphalyam — fruition, becoming fruitful
      sa- (with) + phala (fruit) + -ya (abstract). Birth, education, austerity, sight — each one becomes a phala-bearer only on meeting Kṛṣṇa. Gauḍīyas read sāphalya as the same condition kārtsnyena named in verse 9.
    • śreyasām — of (all) benefits
      Genitive plural of śreyas (highest good). Gauḍīyas distinguish preyas (immediately pleasant) from śreyas (ultimately beneficial), and within śreyas they hold prema-bhakti as the topmost. The sages name Kṛṣṇa as the śreyasām paraḥ — beyond even the standard śreyas-mokṣa.
    • saṅgamya — by obtaining association
      From sam + √gam (to go together). The saṅga of saṅga-saṅgatī. Gauḍīyas treat satāṁ saṅga (SB 3.25.25) as the seed of all spiritual progress — exactly what this gerund names.
    Today our birth, education, austerity and vision have all become perfect because we have been able to associate with You, the goal of all saintly persons. Indeed, You Yourself are the ultimate, supreme blessing.
    Purport

    The sages here contrast their respect for the Lord with His reciprocal worship of them. Lord Kṛṣṇa honors brāhmaṇas as a means of instructing less intelligent men, whereas He is in fact absolutely independent. The brāhmaṇas who worship Him, on the other hand, benefit themselves more than they can imagine.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Today our birth, education, austerity and vision have all become perfect because we have been able to associate with You, the goal of all saintly persons. Indeed, You Yourself are the ultimate, supreme blessing.
    Commentary

    Our knowledge, austerity and eye have become successful today on our attaining association with you, the very form of the ultimate goal (sad gatya), because you are the ultimate limit of auspiciousness (sreyasam parah antah).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Let that be. Now we will reveal the bliss in our hearts by thinking of your inconceivable nature. Today, at this time, you reveal yourself as Svayam Bhagavān, without giving up the qualities we mentioned. Later Devakī will say avatīrṇau kilādya me: taking birth from me, you have now descended to this world. (SB 10.85.30) Today our births have been successful with study of the Vedas, spiritual knowledge of what is not visible in this world arising from actions (tapasaḥ), and knowledge of what is visible in this world (dṛśaḥ). What did we do? We have associated with you along with the supreme shelter of your devotees (sad-gatyā). “You have realized Brahman. You have seen my remarkable appearances in this world. Why then do you describe your birth as successful at the time of my appearance in the world?” You alone are the best of all human goals. You are the highest. Uddhava said: yan martya-līlaupayikaṁ sva-yoga- māyā-balaṁ darśayatā gṛhītam vismāpanaṁ svasya ca saubhagarddheḥ paraṁ padaṁ bhūṣaṇa-bhūṣaṇāṅgam Kṛṣṇa possesses that form suitable for human pastimes to show the full capacity of his yoga-māyā. That form astonishes even the lord of Vaikuṇṭha. It is the pinnacle of auspicious qualities and enhances the beauty of his ornaments. SB 3.2.12

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Today our birth is successful, and spiritual and material knowledge and sva-dharma have become successful. Or today we have taken birth, because our birth is successful. It is otherwise useless, because of lack of knowledge. The various successes are mentioned starting with birth and ending with seeing the Lord (dṛk). Tapas is the cause of seeing the Lord. The Lord is to be attained by the devotees (sad-gatyā). He is the highest end (antaḥ) of what is beneficial. Or being fixed in you (yad antaḥ) brings the highest prema (paraḥ) for your lotus feet--among all beneficial things (śreyasām). That is attained by your mercy.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The sages confess: every credential they brought — birth, learning, austerity, the trained eye — was only a coin waiting for the kiosk of Your darśana. Today the kiosk opened. Kṛṣṇa is the redemption-point of every spiritual asset; meeting Him is what makes them count.

    Stories
    Nārada's first life

    Nārada, in SB 1.5–6, recounts that in his previous life as a maidservant's son he had received the remnants of itinerant Vaiṣṇavas — and that one meal, taken with bhakti, redirected his entire trajectory.

    Gauḍīyas read his story as the proof of this verse: birth and education count only as they converge on sat-saṅga.

    Important Words
    • yoga-māyayā — by His internal illusory potency
      yoga (joining) + māyā (potency). Bhagavān's antaraṅga-śakti. Gauḍīyas sharply distinguish yoga-māyā (internal, enables līlā) from mahā-māyā (external, binds the conditioned soul). The same word, two completely different functions.
    • ācchanna-mahimne — to Him whose glories are covered
      ā + √chad (to cover) + mahiman (greatness). His glories are not absent — they are covered, on purpose. Gauḍīyas treat this as a positive feature, not a deficiency: covered greatness is what permits sakhya and vātsalya to operate.
    • akuṇṭha-medhase — whose intelligence is unrestricted
      Same compound as verse 14, here in dative. The sages return to the phrase deliberately — they began by being confused; they end by saluting the unrestricted intelligence that produced the confusion.
    • parama-ātmane — to the Supersoul
      parama (supreme) + ātman (Self). Gauḍīyas distinguish the three aspects of the Absolute — brahman, paramātmā, bhagavān — and read paramātmā as Bhagavān's localized aspect in every heart. The sages address Kṛṣṇa as the Person who is also the inner Witness.
    Let us offer obeisances unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the infinitely intelligent Supersoul, who has disguised His greatness through His mystic Yoga-māyā.
    Purport

    Apart from any future profit to be obtained from worshiping the Supreme Lord, it is every person’s most essential obligation to bow down to Him as an acknowledgement of one’s dependence and servitude. Lord Kṛṣṇa recommends, man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru mām evaiṣyasi yuktvaivam ātmānaṁ mat-parāyaṇaḥ “Engage your mind always in thinking of Me, become My devotee, offer obeisances to Me and worship Me. Being completely absorbed in Me, surely you will come to Me.” ( Bg. 9.34 )

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Let us offer obeisances unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, the infinitely intelligent Supersoul, who has disguised His greatness through His mystic Yogamāyā.
    Commentary

    Therefore you may praise us or offer respects to us to teach the common man, but we will still offer our respects to you, our worshipable lord. Thus they recite this verse.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Out of great devotion, with astonishment at Kṛṣṇa’s greatness, the sages offer respects. The prayer is directly to Kṛṣṇa expressing “We offer respects to you (tubhyam).” However the sages say, “We offer respects to him (tasmai).” Because of appearance of great devotion they indicate that he is beyond everyone’s understanding and vision (tasmai), since he is Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa (bhagavate), superior to all others, with unlimited intelligence (akuṇṭha-medhase). “But if I always have unlimited intelligence, and am superior to all, why are you not always situated in knowledge?” Your greatness is covered by your yoga-māyā. Nāhaṁ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyāsamāvṛtaḥ: covered by my yogamāyā I am not revealed to all. (BG 7.25) They previously said that they were bewildered by his māyā in verse 16. “How did you get knowledge at this time?” You are Paramātmā: by your merciful inspiration we have developed knowledge of you.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Out of great devotion, thinking themsels most fortunate, the sages offer respects. They do not directly say “We offer respects to you,” out of great devotion. Your greatness is not covered even by your extraordinary yoga-māyā, since you reveal unlimited powers. Or you cover your greatness by your yoga-māyā. Or you cover your greatness, giving mercy (māyā) by which devotees can meet you (yoga). Therefore you are dearest to everyone (paramātmane).

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A sun behind a curtain still warms the room. The sages bow not to the visible boy in the assembly but to the Person whose glories yoga-māyā has drawn a curtain over — knowing the warmth they receive is direct contact with the sun, not with the curtain.

    Stories
    Yoga-māyā at the rāsa-līlā

    In SB 10.29, when the gopīs come to Kṛṣṇa under the autumn moon, yoga-māyā arranges the entire scene so that the gopīs experience Him without the inhibitions of His aiśvarya.

    Gauḍīyas use this to read the verse: yoga-māyā does not hide Bhagavān from devotees, but adjusts what they see so that mādhurya-rasa can flow.

      eka (one, together) + ārāma (enjoyment, pleasure-garden). The Vṛṣṇis enjoy in unison with Kṛṣṇa. Gauḍīyas read this as a marker of intimate līlā — and exactly therefore as the cover under which His aiśvarya is hidden from them.
    • javanikā — curtain
      From java (speed) — a curtain that moves quickly. The technical word for a stage-curtain in Sanskrit drama. Bhagavān's līlā is staged; māyā is the curtain whose movements time the rasa.
    • kālam — time
      Kṛṣṇa as kāla — the same self-disclosure He makes in BG 11.32, kālo 'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt. Paired with īśvaram in the verse. Gauḍīyas note that the Person familiar to the Vṛṣṇis as 'cousin' is also the Time that swallows all kings.
    • ātmānam — the Supreme Soul
      ātman as Bhagavān's Self, here qualified by kālam īśvaram. Gauḍīyas read ātmā in this verse not as the impersonal self but as the Soul of all souls — paramātmā, equivalent to Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa.
    Neither these kings nor even the Vṛṣṇis, who enjoy Your intimate association, know You as the Soul of all existence, the force of time and the supreme controller. For them You are covered by the curtain of Māyā.
    Purport

    Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī explains that Lord Kṛṣṇa’s family, the Vṛṣṇis, were too familiar with Him to realize that He is the Supersoul residing in the heart of every created being. And those kings at Kurukṣetra who were not devotees of Kṛṣṇa could not recognize Him as time, the annihilator of everything. Devotees and nondevotees are both covered by Māyā, but in different ways. For the materialists Māyā is illusion, but for the Vaiṣṇavas she acts as Yoga-māyā, the internal potency who covers their awareness of the Supreme Lord’s majesty and engages them in His eternal pleasure pastimes.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Neither these kings nor even the Vṛṣṇis, who enjoy Your intimate association, know You as the Soul of all existence, the force of time and the supreme controller. For them You are covered by the curtain of Māyā.
    Commentary

    The Vrsnis do not know you, who are the object of the intense affection, as the Lord, having sat on the same seat or bed with you, and the kings do not know you, who destroys them as time, as the Lord. Why? Because you are covered by the screen of maya, a covering of their knowledge. It should be concluded however that it is ignorance which covers the kings and yogamaya which covers the Vrsnis.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Who are we, so far from you? Those who are near you, even the kings, and even the Vṛṣṇis, who take you as their only pleasure, do not know you as Svayam Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa. They cannot realize the real extent of your greatness. “What is the cause of their not realizing me, filled with all powers, since I remain in a manifested form?” You are covered by māyā. How can it cover all my powers? It is a screen: those who are your intimate associates can realize your greatness by your desire. They describe his greatness. You are Brahman (ātmanam). You impel all beings (kalayati -kālam) as antaryāmī. You are Svayam Bhagavān (īśvaram).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The people gathered here are more fortunate than us sages. They take pleasure only in you (ekārāmāḥ). They do not know you as all pervading Brahman (ātmanam), as fearful time, destroying everything, or as the Lord. They know you as the son of Devakī, protector of everyone, and the dearest. Why? You are covered by a curtain of māyā, since you manifest your unlimited qualities as bhagavān.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A son growing up with his father may know him as 'papa' but never as the celebrated jurist of the city. The Vṛṣṇis and the Pāṇḍavas live with Kṛṣṇa, share His bed and His war, but the curtain of māyā keeps Him in domestic costume. The sages, arriving from outside the household, name what the household cannot quite name from inside.

    Stories
    Arjuna's bewilderment in BG 11

    Arjuna, the most intimate friend, asks Kṛṣṇa to show him the Universal Form (BG 11) and is undone by it. Afterward he says, sakheti matvā prasabhaṁ yad uktam — thinking of You as a friend, I have addressed You presumptuously (11.41–42).

    Gauḍīyas read Arjuna's confession as the very condition this verse describes: intimacy that did not register the aiśvarya, until yoga-māyā briefly lifted the curtain.

    Important Words
    • smṛti-upaplavāt — due to the disruption of memory
      smṛti (memory) + upaplava (overflow, disruption). The forgetting of one's eternal relationship with Bhagavān. Gauḍīyas treat smṛti as a technical term: nityaḥ kṛṣṇa-smṛti is the goal; the disease is its disruption.
    • nāma-mātreṣu — in things having only names
      nāma (name) + mātra (only, mere). The objects perceived by the dreaming jīva are name-only — they have no substance independent of Bhagavān. Gauḍīyas read this not as Buddhist śūnyatā but as acintya-bhedābheda: real but not standalone.
    • indriya-īhayā — by the activity of the senses
      indriya (sense) + īhā (activity). The senses act and the world appears. Gauḍīyas note that bhakti redirects the senses (hṛṣīkeṇa hṛṣīkeśa-sevanaṁ bhaktir ucyate, Nārada-pañcarātra), turning indriya-īhā from world-making into Kṛṣṇa-service.
    • guṇa-tattva-dṛk — whose vision is of secondary reality
      guṇa (secondary, modifying) + tattva (reality) + dṛś (vision). The dreamer's eye sees the secondary. Gauḍīyas treat the goal as the recovery of paramārtha-dṛṣṭi — seeing the Person who underlies the guṇas.
    A sleeping person imagines an alternative reality for himself and, seeing himself as having various names and forms, forgets his waking identity, which is distinct from the dream. Similarly, the senses of one whose consciousness is bewildered by illusion perceive only the names and forms of material objects. Thus such a person loses his memory and cannot know You.
    Purport

    Just as a person’s dream is a secondary reality created from the stock of his memories and desires, so this universe exists as the inferior creation of the Supreme Lord, in no real way separate from Him. And just as the person who awakens from sleep experiences the higher reality of his waking life, so the Supreme Lord also has His distinct, higher reality beyond everything we know of this world. In His own words, mayā tatam idaṁ sarvaṁ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni na cāhaṁ teṣv avasthitaḥ na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamātmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ “By Me, in My unmanifested form, this entire universe is pervaded. All beings are in Me, but I am not in them. And yet everything that is created does not rest in Me. Behold My mystic opulence! Although I am the maintainer of all living entities and although I am everything, I am not part of this cosmic manifestation, for My Self is the very source of creation.” (Bg. 9.4-5)

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    A sleeping person imagines an alternative reality for himself and, seeing himself as having various names and forms, forgets his waking identity, which is distinct from the dream. Similarly, the senses of one whose consciousness is bewildered by illusion perceive only the names and forms of material objects. Thus such a person loses his memory and cannot know You.
    Commentary

    People do not know that you are one with the universe with its many names and forms and also superior to it. This is explained using an example in two verses. Just as a man dreaming sees as real the objects in the dream, and knows many names and forms of tiger, snake and king appearing with senses such as the ear, tan matras such as form an sound, and names, but does not know himself who has become those forms, and rather knows something other than his real form, so the ignorant man bewildered by maya through action of the senses like the ear, knows you by the names of deva or man, and with material form and qualities. He does not know your true form, separate from the many names and forms that you assume as the universe, because of loss of intelligence.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Others do not know you. Two verses explain. Verses 22 onwards can be explained in another way. How does the Lord act is this way? He is not covered by māyā. We offer respects to the Lord who is not covered (acchanna) by his extraordinary āvaraṇa-śakti (material māyā), since he manifests unlimited powers. Or, we offer respects to the Lord who covers his powers by his mercy (māyayā) so that he can have intimate relationships (yoga) with his devotees (sva). Therefore he is most dear to all (paramātmane). The persons present at this place are more fortunate than us. That is explained in verse 23. Those who have gathered here and the intimate Vṛṣṇis who are superior to the others, do not see the Lord to be covered by a screen of māyā. Rather they see him uncovered, because he manifests his svarūpa to them. Realizing his uncovered form, they do not see his form as impersonal Brahman (ātmanam). Surpassing that, realizing his personal form, they do not even see his form as Paramātmā (kālam). Surpassing that, realizing the form of Bhagavān, the source of all other forms, they do not see his form as the Supreme Lord. Surpassing all those realization of bliss in those forms one after the other, they realize him as the lord of his affectionate friends. itthaṁ satāṁ brahma-sukhānubhūtyā dāsyaṁ gatānāṁ para-daivatena māyāśritānāṁ nara-dārakeṇa sākaṁ vijahruḥ kṛta-puṇya-puṣjāḥ In this way with an abundance of splendor caused by Kṛṣṇa, they played with him, though he is pure consciousness or happiness known as Brahman for the jṣānīs, the Supreme Lord for the devotees with dāsya-bhāva and an ordinary human child for those covered by material illusion.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The devotee is unbewildered by māyā, which incites the senses to objects and forms, because of absorption in scriptures. Others do not know you. That is explained in these two verses. A sleeping person sees himself as names, which are false (nāma-mātra), because the image appears through the senses (indriyābhātam). Or some person among the Vṛṣṇis, even while sleeping, knows you, the Lord (ātmānam), correctly (yathā), and not anything else (rahitam param), because he directly realizes (paśyati) your qualities like mercy, which are real and eternal (guṇa-tattva-dṛk). He knows you who reveal yourself (ābhātam) in the senses, objects (mātra) and all your names. Or he knows you, manifested as Śyamasundara, with senses, forms and names, not devoid of these as Brahman. People are not bewildered about you (vibhama-cittaḥ) because of māyā, which activates (īhayā) the senses in perceiving objects and forms visibly (nāma). Rather they constantly realize you through Vedas and smṛtis (veda-smṛtyupaplavāt).

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A dreaming man wears a different name and walks a different street and forgets his real bed. Daybreak doesn't argue him out of the dream; it simply ends it. The conditioned soul perceives only names-and-forms because his consciousness is dreaming; only smṛti — the breaking of the dream — restores Kṛṣṇa to view.

    Stories
    Bharata as a deer

    Bharata Mahārāja, again (SB 5.7–14), forgets his identity entirely and lives as a deer — the dream is total. When he is reborn as Jaḍa Bharata, the dream's smṛti-upaplava (the disruption of memory) begins to mend; he refuses to call the body or its relations 'mine.'

    Gauḍīyas treat his trajectory as the case-study of this verse: the soul forgets, then by Bhagavān's grace remembers.

    Ajāmila on his deathbed

    Ajāmila (SB 6.1–3) is the dreaming man who, by uttering the name 'Nārāyaṇa' in the last hour, briefly wakes up. Smṛti returns; the dream breaks; the Viṣṇu-dūtas claim him.

    Gauḍīyas read his story as the operational hope inside this verse — even the longest dream can be ended by the name.

    Important Words
    • agha-ogha-marṣa — which undoes the flood of sins
      agha (sin) + ogha (flood) + marṣa (forbearing, undoing). Bhagavān's feet are not just clean — they unmake the accumulation of sin. Gauḍīyas note the river-imagery: ogha matches the Ganges, marṣa matches its flow.
    • tīrtha-āspadam — the source of the holy pilgrimage site
      tīrtha + āspada (resting place, source). The feet are the source-point of the tīrtha — the doctrine of verse 11 brought to its furthest end: not only is the sādhu the real tīrtha, but Bhagavān's feet are the tīrtha's tīrtha.
    • utsikta-bhakti — fully developed devotional service
      ut-sikta (poured upon, sprinkled out, fully ripened) + bhakti. Bhakti at its full pour. Gauḍīyas read this as a near-synonym for prema-bhakti — the stage at which bhakti has overflowed the disciplinary banks.
    • jīva-kośāḥ — the external covering of the individual soul
      jīva (individual soul) + kośa (sheath, covering). The mind-shaped covering that needs to be destroyed for the jīva to meet Bhagavān. Gauḍīyas read kośa-bheda not as Advaitin merging but as the lifting of the covering so the eternal servant may serve.
    • anugṛhāṇa — please show mercy
      anu + √grah (to seize, accept). To grasp toward, to bestow grace. Gauḍīyas treat anugraha as the active form of kṛpā: not passive favor but Bhagavān's reaching out. The sages, having said so much, end the speech with this imperative.
    Today we have directly seen Your feet, the source of the holy Ganges, which washes away volumes of sins. Perfected yogīs can at best meditate upon Your feet within their hearts. But only those who render You wholehearted devotional service and in this way vanquish the soul’s covering — the material mind — attain You as their final destination. Therefore kindly show mercy to us, Your devotees.
    Purport

    The holy river Ganges has the power to destroy all sorts of sinful reactions because she originates at the Lord’s lotus feet and thus contains the dust of His feet. Explaining this verse, Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī says, “If the Lord might advise the sages that they need not concern themselves with devotional practices because they are already far advanced in spiritual knowledge and austerity, they hereby respectfully decline such a suggestion, pointing out that only those yogīs who have destroyed their material mind and ego by surrendering to Kṛṣṇa in pure devotional service can attain full perfection. They conclude by praying to the Lord that He favor them in the most merciful way by making them His devotees.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Today we have directly seen Your feet, the source of the holy Ganges, which washes away volumes of sins. Perfected yogīs can at best meditate upon Your feet within their hearts. But only those who render You wholehearted devotional service and in this way vanquish the soul's covering—the material mind—attain You as their final destination. Therefore kindly show mercy to us, Your devotees.
    Commentary

    "We who are explaining this knowledge are your devotees, for seeing you in this way is not possible without devotion. We see your lotus feet which are the shelter of holy places like the Ganga which destroy (marsa) all sins (agha) and are placed in the heart by advanced methods of yoga through meditation but not seen." "That may be, but to destroy the subtle body, jnana is necessary." "Those whose subtle bodies (jiva kosa) containing desires are destroyed by intense devotion attain the goal and not others. Therefore knowing us to be devotees, please give us mercy."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The sages conclude. Today we have seen the feet of you who are rarely realized. Today our lives have become successful since those feet are the highest sādhana (method of attainment) and sādhya (attainment). This is explained by two descriptive phrases. Your feet are the origin of the holy Gaṅgā which destroys a host of sins which make persons inimical to your bhakti. The most mature yogīs and ātmārāmas place those feet in their hearts. “Why is the realization of the ātmārāma disrespected and bhakti praised?” Bhakti destroys the material mind. Another version has apahṛta instead of apahata, but the meaning is the same. Those who have destroyed the coverings on the jīva by intense bhakti, attain you. Making them devotees, be merciful to them, so that they can constantly see you.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Therefore, show such mercy to us today. O supreme person (ādya)! Or today, on this day that the people of Vraja have come, we have seen the feet of the Lord who manifests his unlimted glories (tasya). Therefore be merciful to us. Your feet are rarely seen. They are the shelter of all tīrthas since they have the power of the Gaṅgā which is all tīrthas. Or your feet are most purifying. Gaṅgā is hard to attain. Your feet, the shelter of the Gaṅgā, are even harder to attain. Moreove Sanaka and others, advanced yogīs, simply keep those feet in their hearts. Those who have destroyed the coverings on the jīva, the false conceptsion of knowledge etc. (āśaya) by bhakti attain Vaikuṇṭha (bhavad-gatim). “Since you are offenders, propagating māyāvāda, mīmāṁsa, sāṅkhya, all of which are without concepts of God, how can I show you mercy?” You forgive all offenses (aghaugha-marṣa).

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The sages, having walked through the doctrinal map of two dozen verses, end at the feet themselves: not as conclusion but as the actual washing place from which the Ganges issues. Perfected yogis hold these feet in meditation; only undivided bhakti, melting the kośa, lands a soul among them. The whole speech bends toward the touch of those feet.

    Stories
    Bhagīratha and the Ganges

    The Mahābhārata and Bhāgavatam (SB 9.9) record that the Ganges descends from Viṣṇu's foot (washed by Brahmā in SB 8.21) and is brought to earth by Bhagīratha's tapas to liberate his ancestors.

    Gauḍīyas read the verse's tīrtha-āspadam — the source of the holy pilgrimage site — as referring to that very descent: the foot is the source of the river that is the source of every tīrtha.

    Caitanya's feet at Jagannātha Purī

    Caitanya-caritāmṛta records that the Bhaṭṭācārya, Rāya Rāmānanda, and finally Sārvabhauma surrendered when they touched Mahāprabhu's feet. The feet of Bhagavān, in any age, function as the verse names — agha-ogha-marṣa, washing the floods of sin.

    Gauḍīyas read this verse as the foundational charter for caraṇa-sevā.

    Important Words
    • dāśārham — Kṛṣṇa, the descendant of Daśārha
      Daśārha was an ancestor in the Yadu line. Gauḍīyas note that Kṛṣṇa's many vamśa-titles — Dāśārha, Vṛṣṇi-vīra, Yadu-nandana — register that He has voluntarily entered into a human lineage; the names anchor His incarnation in actual genealogy.
    • anujñāpya — having taken permission to leave
      anu + √jñā in causative + ya. The sādhu does not depart without permission. Gauḍīyas treat anujñā as a small but important sign of saṅga-dharma: the relationship is honored on both ends of the visit.
    • rāja-ṛṣe — O sage among kings
      Address to Parīkṣit. The Bhāgavatam never lets the reader forget that this entire transmission is happening between Śuka and a king-sage. Gauḍīyas read Parīkṣit as the model śrotā — the perfect listener of hari-kathā in his last seven days.
    • āśramān — to the hermitages
      From ā + √śram (to exert). The disciplined retreats. Gauḍīyas note that the āśrama is not anti-world but a workshop for the world's renewal: ṛṣis go back to āśramas to refill what they spend in sat-saṅga.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus spoken, O wise king, the sages then took leave of Lord Dāśārha, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Yudhiṣṭhira and prepared to depart for their āśramas.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Having thus spoken, O wise king, the sages then took leave of Lord Dāśārha, Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Yudhiṣṭhira and prepared to depart for their āśramas.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Saying this special information, they then asked permission to depart from Svayam Bhagavān who had appeared in the Dāśārha family, for Dhratrāṣtṛa and Yudhiṣṭhira. Dhṛtarāṣṭra is mentioned because he was sitting there, was blind, was the younger brother of Vyāsa, and made them remember Yudhiṣṭhira. The sages desired to return home, to teach bhakti their disciples and followers in their āśramas, according to the desire of the Lord. O sage among kings! You know such desires.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Saying this special information, or asking permission to depart from Svayam Bhagavān who had appeared in the Dāśārha family to manifest his powers. The sages wanted to return to their places to give instructions of bhakti to their students and followers. O sage among kings! You know the nature of the sages.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    After the discourse, the sages do not linger to be praised — they ask leave and turn toward their āśramas, like rivers that, having delivered their water to the sea, climb back into the clouds to fall as rain elsewhere. The mark of a sādhu is that he keeps moving toward the next sevā.

    Important Words
    • vasudevaḥ — Vasudeva
      Father of Kṛṣṇa, named ānakadundubhi (drums of the gods sounded at his birth). Gauḍīyas treat him as the standing instance of vātsalya from the father's side, complementary to Yaśodā's vātsalya in Vraja.
    • upasaṅgṛhya — taking hold of their feet
      upa + sam + √grah. The technical word for receiving the dust of the feet. Gauḍīyas read pādārcana / pāda-saṅgrahaṇa as a non-negotiable feature of approaching a brāhmaṇa-sage.
    • su-yantritaḥ — very carefully composed
      su- + yantrita (controlled, restrained). Vasudeva speaks with restraint. Gauḍīyas note that vāk-tapas (austerity of speech, BG 17.15) is the prerequisite for serious spiritual inquiry — not the casual chat.
    • praṇamya — bowing down
      Gerund of pra + √nam. Again the body leads — bow first, speak second. Gauḍīyas read praṇāma as the entry-rite of every encounter with a Vaiṣṇava.
    Seeing that they were about to leave, the renowned Vasudeva approached the sages. After bowing down to them and touching their feet, he spoke to them with carefully chosen words.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Seeing that they were about to leave, the renowned Vasudeva approached the sages. After bowing down to them and touching their feet, he spoke to them with carefully chosen words.
    Commentary

    Grasping their feet, Vasudeva spoke. The sandhi of bibhase with idam (bibhasedam) is poetic license. "Such sages are difficult to bring, even if invited. The doubts in my heard cannot be destroyed except by them. Therefore now I should ask them my questions."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Knowing the intention of the sages to leave (tat vīkṣya), Vasudeva, famous because he was the father of the Lord, went to them. Following human pastimes like the Lord, he offered respects and spoke with the greatest courtesy (suyantritaḥ) in order to give bliss to Kṛṣna and the people by crediting to the Lord his proper fame.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Knowing the intention of the sages to leave (tat vīkṣya), Vasudeva, though famous because he was the father of the Lord, went to them. Or he went to them, with the intention of his future fame. He spoke humbly (suyantritaḥ).

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Vasudeva, the father of Bhagavān Himself, does not stand on rank. He bows, takes the dust of the ṛṣis' feet, and speaks with carefully composed words. The man who fathered God models the verse just spoken: the brāhmaṇa is the form Bhagavān has chosen to be honored through.

    Stories
    Vasudeva carrying the infant Kṛṣṇa

    In SB 10.3, on the night of Kṛṣṇa's birth, Vasudeva carries the newborn through the storm-swollen Yamunā to Gokula. The Yamunā parts for him, Śeṣa shelters him.

    Gauḍīyas hold Vasudeva as the original father-devotee, whose humility before sages now — though he has fathered the Lord — is the same humility that earned him fatherhood in the first place.

    Important Words
    • nirhāraḥ — purging, removal
      From nir- (out) + √hṛ (to take). The phrase karmaṇā karma-nirhāraḥ frames the rest of the chapter. Gauḍīyas read it as pointing toward yajña-as-bhakti: karma performed as worship of Viṣṇu (verse 35) is the karma that dissolves prior karma — the classical karma-yoga reading of BG 3.9, yajñārthāt karmaṇaḥ.
    • sarva-devebhyaḥ — to all the demigods
      Vasudeva addresses the sages as comprising all the demigods. Gauḍīyas note that the Vaiṣṇava ṛṣi is treated as comprehending all deva-tattva — pūjā of the sādhu is implicit pūjā of every demigod (cf. SB 4.31.14).
    • śrotum arhatha — please be willing to hear me
      śrotum (to hear) + arhatha (you are worthy). Polite request. Gauḍīyas note that the householder approaching the sage does not demand instruction — he asks to be heard, an inversion that itself constitutes saṅga-dharma.
    • ucyatām — please say
      Passive imperative of √vac. The standard śiṣya-question form. Gauḍīyas note that the Bhāgavatam's many great teachings (BG 1.21–22; SB 1.1.1) issue from exactly this passive-imperative — an open hand toward the speaker.
    Śrī Vasudeva said: Obeisances to you, the residence of all the demigods. Please hear me, O sages. Kindly tell us how the reactions of one’s work can be counteracted by further work.
    Purport

    Here Vasudeva addresses the sages as “the residence of all the demigods.” His statement is confirmed in the authoritative śruti-mantras, which declare, yāvatīr vai devatās tāḥ sarvā veda-vidi brāhmaṇe vasanti: “Whatever demigods exist, all reside in a brāhmaṇa who knows the Veda. ”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śrī Vasudeva said: Obeisances to you, the residence of all the demigods. Please hear me, O sages. Kindly tell us how the reactions of one's work can be counteracted by further work.
    Commentary

    " I offer respects to you, the form of all the devatas." This shown in sruti which says, "All the devatas reside in the brahmana who knows the Vedas." "Please describe how I can destroy the bondage of karma by action, because, being greatly attached to house, children and wives, I am not qualified for jnana or bhakti."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Though he knew the answer, he asked the sages in order to protect codes of respect by taking proof from persons qualified to teach.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I offer respects to you (vaḥ). He first offers respects out of devotion in order to make a request. O sages! You are omniscient! Therefore you should listen to me. You are qualified. I make this request. Though he knows the answer he asks them. At that holy place he wanted the assembled kings, sages and relatives to follow what the sages said, with a desire for a festive sacrifice.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Vasudeva, knowing that karma drags the karmī between two birth-banks, asks the sages the question of how karma itself might be set against karma — like a man with a thorn in his foot asking which other thorn would pull this one out. The whole second half of the chapter is the sages' answer.

    Important Words
    • arbhakam — a boy
      From arbha (small, weak). The very word Yaśodā would use. Gauḍīyas treat the appearance of arbhaka here as evidence that vātsalya-māyā operates on Vasudeva as well as Yaśodā — though differently — and is itself a gift of Kṛṣṇa to His own parents.
    • bubhutsayā — with the desire of learning
      Desiderative of √budh (to know). Vasudeva is genuinely seeking. Gauḍīyas read bubhutsā as the right disposition of a śiṣya — the verb-form itself encodes the leaning forward.
    • śreyaḥ — the highest good
      The classical śreyas — paired in the verse with ātmanaḥ (for himself). Gauḍīyas note that the Bhāgavatam's whole frame is set by such questions — beginning with the Naimiṣāraṇya sages (SB 1.1.9, śreyaḥ etan na pṛcchāmaḥ) and now repeated by Vasudeva.
    • matvā — thinking
      Gerund of √man. The verb itself — matvā arbhakam — is the diagnostic. Vasudeva thinks-Kṛṣṇa-a-boy, and that thinking is what makes the question possible. Gauḍīyas read this as the operation of yoga-māyā in vātsalya-rasa.
    Śrī Nārada Muni said: O brāhmaṇas, it is not so amazing that in his eagerness to know, Vasudeva has asked us about his ultimate benefit, for he considers Kṛṣṇa a mere boy.
    Purport

    Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī relates Nārada’s thoughts: Śrī Nārada understood how Vasudeva, in line with his mood of pretending to be an ordinary householder, asked the sages about karma-yoga, although he had already attained spiritual goals even great yogīs and ṛṣis cannot achieve. But Nārada was still concerned that Vasudeva might create an awkward mood by treating Lord Kṛṣṇa as a mere child in the presence of all the sages. Nārada and the other sages felt obliged to maintain their attitude of reverence toward Lord Kṛṣṇa, so how could they ignore Him and presume to answer Vasudeva themselves? To avoid this embarrassment, Nārada took this opportunity to remind everyone present of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s absolute supremacy.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śrī Nārada Muni said: O brāhmaṇas, it is not so amazing that in his eagerness to know, Vasudeva has asked us about his ultimate benefit, for he considers Kṛṣṇa a mere boy.
    Commentary

    The sages were astonished "Oh, he is the father of the Lord, and thinks himself fallen in the material world. Of, if he is asking for the benefit of others, why does he give up Krsna and ask us?" To answer them, Narada spoke this verse. "It is not surprising that Vasudeva, thinking of Krsna as his son (arbakam), not the Lord, asks what is beneficial for himself (atmanah) from us."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “Why does Kṛṣṇa’s father, who has attained good fortune desired by us, but hard to attain, ask about something other than Kṛṣṇa? If he asks, how can he give up Kṛṣṇa and ask someone else?” Astonished the sages were silent. Though knowing Vasudeva’s intention which was previously explained, Nārada spoke as if intolerant of Vasudeva’s question. Since as Vasudeva was well versed in Kṛṣṇa’s powers, and knew the path of the highest good, unlike Nanda who was absorbed in Kṛṣṇa’s sweetness, asking this question was part of his human pastimes in order to spread his son’s sattvika glories. That question was very insignificant for the Lord who possessed the highest glories. Or, Svayam Bhagavān reveals his pastimes to hide his power to some degree. This may however produce some misunderstanding. If we attend to this, people will become bewildered. Therefore it is suitable that I show the Lord’s powers, on the pretext of criticizing Vasudeva. He speaks in four verses. In the first two verses he criticizes Vasudeva for bewildering people. In the second two verses he praises Kṛṣṇa as the height of human goals and knowledge. Vasudeva considered Kṛṣṇa to be a material son (arbhakam) and asked about another means of attain the highest goal. Giving up Kṛṣṇa who is beside him, Vasudeva asked us.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The sages were astonished because Vasudeva in the presence of the supreme Lord, forgetting the Lord’s powers because of great affection, asked them a question. Knowing the greatness of bhakti, Nārada speaks to them with affection. This is not even surprising (na api citram). Citsukha has a version with na ati-citram. Vasudeve thinks that Kṛṣna, though the supreme Lord, is a boy, out of affection.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    A grandmother lives with the king of the world dressed as her grandson and asks the neighbors how to obtain the king's favor. Nārada smiles at Vasudeva's question, not because it is foolish but because intimacy has rearranged the categories: the questioner does not see that he is asking the sages about the one whose father he is.

    Stories
    Yaśodā binding Kṛṣṇa

    Yaśodā in SB 10.9 binds Kṛṣṇa with the rope — Bhagavān whom no one binds, bound by a mother who sees Him as her boy. Vātsalya is the same yoga-māyā at work that Nārada here describes.

    Gauḍīyas read Nārada's smile as the smile of one who knows that vātsalya is not a deficit of theology — it is the deepest theology in its embodied form.

    Important Words
    • sannikarṣaḥ — proximity, closeness
      sam + ni + √kṛṣ (to draw). The very condition of being close. Gauḍīyas note that sannikarṣa to Bhagavān is meant to ripen into rāgānuga; but it can also, in the conditioned soul, ripen into anādara — dullness toward what is near.
    • anādaraṇa — disregard
      an- (not) + ādara (respect). The standing failure of human beings vis-à-vis what is close at hand. Gauḍīyas treat anādara as the symptom of forgotten smṛti — verse 24–25's smṛty-upaplava in social-emotional form.
    • gāṅgam — of the Ganges
      From gaṅgā. Nārada chooses the holiest river for the image precisely because the failure of treating it as merely water is the same failure that this chapter has named four times now (verses 11, 13, 26, 31).
    • śuddhaye — for purification
      Dative of śuddhi (purification). The motive that drives the absurd trip elsewhere. Gauḍīyas note that proper śuddhi is achieved by Bhagavān's name and feet — both already present in Vasudeva's house.
    In this world familiarity breeds contempt. For example, one who lives on the banks of the Ganges might travel to some other body of water to be purified.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    In this world familiarity breeds contempt. For example, one who lives on the banks of the Ganges might travel to some other body of water to be purified.
    Commentary

    Indeed, he knew that Krsna was the Lord from his very birth, but living close to him bred familiarity. That is expressed in this verse. Narada knew that the cause of Vasudeva not seeing Krsna as God was Vasudeva’s prema, but at that great gathering he explained things according to the common man’s level, not describing the greatly confidential highest truth about prema. Hearing this verse from Narada, it is certain that Vasudeva would increase his respect for Krsna as the Lord. For men proximity is a cause of lack of reverence (anadara).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The reason for Vasudeva’s conduct is as follows. Instead of atra the word hi is also seen. Sometimes this verse is placed before the previous verse. Vasudeva acts like a normal human being in his pastimes and thus shows familiarity and lack of respect. Rejecting Gaṅgā water one goes to the water of another holy place for purification.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Affection reduces the respect. An example is given. When one is always close to another person out of affection it causes lack of respect. Or if one is constantly and completely attracted to someone, having great affection (sannikarṣaḥ) it causes lack of respect. A person living on the Gaṅgā gives up Gaṅgā water and goes to other water.
