    Important Words
    • anubhūtiḥ — awareness
      anu + √bhū (to be after, become). Bhagavān's consciousness, technical term for divine cit. Gauḍīyas read His anubhūti as svarūpa-jñāna — He is fully self-aware always, regardless of the līlā He is enacting.
    • advitīyam — without a second
      a- (not) + dvitīya (second). Famous Upaniṣadic term (Chāndogya 6.2.1 — ekam evādvitīyam). Gauḍīyas read this not in Advaitin merging-monism but as the Vaiṣṇava reading: Bhagavān is one without a second, and yet His energies and His devotees are eternally distinct from and dependent on Him.
    • sūryam iva — like the sun
      The standard image of an uncovered cause behind apparent coverings. Gauḍīyas note that this image runs through SB and the Upaniṣads, and was deployed by Caitanya in His teachings to Rūpa Gosvāmī (CC Madhya 19) on acintya-bhedābheda.
    • vibhavaiḥ — with His expansions
      From vi + √bhū (to be powerful, expand). The prāṇa and elements are Bhagavān's own vibhavas — His expansions, not foreign agents. Gauḍīyas read this as a doctrinal anti-dualism: even what seems to cover Him is His own.
    The Supreme Lord’s awareness is never disturbed by time, by the creation and destruction of the universe, by changes in its own qualities, or by anything else, whether self-caused or external. But although the consciousness of the Personality of Godhead, who is the supreme one without a second, is never affected by material distress, by the reactions of material work or by the constant flow of nature’s modes, ordinary persons nonetheless think that the Lord is covered by His own creations of prāṇa and other material elements, just as one may think that the sun is covered by clouds, snow or an eclipse.
    Purport

    Things of this world are inevitably destroyed by one means or another. Time itself causes the eventual decay of every created being — a fruit, for instance, which may grow ripe but then must either rot or be eaten. Some things, like lightning, destroy themselves as soon as they are manifested, while others are destroyed suddenly by external agents, as a clay pot is by a hammer. Even in living bodies and other things whose existence continues for some time, there is a constant flux of various qualities that are destroyed and replaced by others. In contrast to all of this, the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s awareness is never disrupted by anything. Only out of ignorance could one imagine Him to be an ordinary human being subject to material conditions. Mortal beings are covered by their entanglement in fruitive activities and their consequent happiness and distress, but the Supreme Lord cannot be covered by what are in fact His own expansions. Analogously, the immense sun is the source of the relatively insignificant phenomena of clouds, snow and eclipses, and so it cannot be covered by them, though the ordinary observer may think that it is.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Lord's awareness is never disturbed by time, by the creation and destruction of the universe, by changes in its own qualities, or by anything else, whether self-caused or external. But although the consciousness of the Personality of Godhead, who is the supreme one without a second, is never affected by material distress, by the reactions of material work or by the constant flow of nature's modes, ordinary persons nonetheless think that the Lord is covered by His own creations of prāṇa and other material elements, just as one may think that the sun is covered by clouds, snow or an eclipse.
    Commentary

    "O most worshippable persons, knowers of brahman, not only Vasudeva is subject to this criticism. Almost all of the people here do not know that Krsna is the supreme lord." This is explained in two verses. The materialistic people (anya) think of Krsna, whose knowledge cannot be destroyed, who is covered by the pranas etc, as one like themselves. (the verb is found in the second verse.) His knowledge cannot be destroyed by time which causes destruction or creation of the universe as with the growth and decay of karkatika fruit,; by his own nature, like lightening which disappears on its own; by means other than himself like a hammer which destroys a clay pot; or by the mode of ignorance, which destroys the universe. He repeats the same idea to strengthen his statement in this verse. His knowledge is not destroyed by suffering such as attachment (klesa), karmas (the cause of suffering), the immediate results of karma in the form of happiness and distress (paripaka), or by the flow of the three modes (guna). But ignorant men think that the Lord, who appeared to be covered (but never controlled) by his own products (sva vibhavaih) of the subtle body made of prana, mind, intelligence, to be a person like themselves, as the sun is covered by its own products in the form of clouds, fog (hima), or by rahu (uparaga) during an eclipse, The sun is the cause of the cloud, because the cloud is made of water and light is the cause of water. Water is the cause of fog. The sun is the cause of rahu because rahu is composed of a portion of darkness in the form of bad habits of evil jivas, and perception of darkness depends on the eye (caused by the sun). According to the Puranas, the sun is the cause of the clouds because fire element is the cause of clouds, and water.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Awareness and manifesting power (anubhūtiḥ) of the Lord as the doer and object of action are not destroyed by creation and destruction of the universe (asya), by time (which causes destruction of the universe), by itself (like lightning which appears and disappears on its own), by something else like the blow of a hammer to a pot, or by qualities being destroyed and changing to other qualities, as in a body. The awareness and powers are eternally existent. The next verse states the opposite condition of the Lord. Kṛṣṇa is without a second (advitīyam) since he alone is Svayam Bhagavān. The descriptive terms are in order of increasing excellence in human terms. Yet ordinary people think he is covered by prāṇas and suffering because of suffering and prāṇas in their associates. Because they suffer, they think Kṛṣṇa is similar to themselves, since everyone thinks in terms of themselves. The sun is king of the planets but seems to be covered by Rāhu. The Lord’s powers are never affected since he does not suffer like the persons present at that place. He is the completely independent (īśvaram) because his knowledge is dependent on himself. He is Kṛṣṇa, without compare (advitīyam) because he alone manifests everything else. Another person thinks the Lord has limited knowledge because of his vibhava (his various forms) and his senses (prāṇa) and his limbs (ādibhiḥ), just as the sun is covered by clouds, snow or an eclipse. The meaning is this. The sun appears to be limited in form by clouds or the eclipse. That is suitable since the cloud is a transformation of vapors of water pulled up by rays of the sun. Snow is also a conglomeration of particles of water pulled up by the sun. Rāhu, the cause of the eclipse, is the form of darkness which dependent on the sun. The Lord’s eyes and other senses are not like that, but are part of his svarūpa or vibhava. Therefore these senses and limbs cannot cover the Lord’s knowledge. Similarly the sun cannot be covered by warmth etc. produced from his svarūpa. Rather the sun is revealed by them. His svarūpa is not covered by time or place, and his knowledge is not covered since his eyes and limbs are also similar to his svarūpa. However, low people will think the opposite. It is said na cāntar na bahir yasya: he has no interior or exterior. SB 10.9.13 nātaḥ paraṁ parama yad bhavataḥ svarūpam ānanda-mātram avikalpam aviddha-varcaḥ Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Lord, is the cause of all causes. He is past, present and future, and he is the movable and immovable. (SB 3.9.3) yo ’nādṛto naraka-bhāgbhir asat-prasaṅgaiḥ: those who are destined to be dispatched to the path of hell neglect your personal form because of speculating on material topics. SB 3.9.4 ye tu tvadīya-caraṇāmbuja-kośa-gandhaṁ jighranti karṇa-vivaraiḥ śruti-vāta-nītam bhaktyā gṛhīta-caraṇaḥ parayā ca teṣāṁ nāpaiṣi nātha hṛdayāmburuhāt sva-puṁsām O master! You do not give up the lotus hearts of your devotees who smell through their ears the fragrance of your lotus bud feet brought by the wind of the Vedas, and take your lotus feet as the greatest treasure through prema-bhakti. SB 3.9.5

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One should not think that Vasudeva does not know the glory of the Lord. A material person does not know about the Lord. The Lord is not disturbed even (vai) by creation, maintenance (ādinā) and destruction though they are huge endeavors (for other people). The Lord has unrestricted knowledge, and has no equal (advitīyam). The series of descriptive terms indicate successively greater reasons for not condering him human. However persons other than Vasudeva, material persons, think the Lord is covered by karmas and suffering, by prāṇas and senses (ādibhiḥ) because of their ripened suffering (sva-vibhavaiḥ). Because they experience pain they think the Lord also experiences pain. Or a person endowed with sufferings and karma (kleśa-karma-paripāka-guṇa-pravāhair), thinks the Lord is covered. But Vasudeva knows the highest manifestation of the Lord but of affection, he forgets. This is the Lord’s mercy. pitarāv upalabdhārthau viditvā puruṣottamaḥ mā bhūd iti nijāṁ māyāṁ tatāna jana-mohinīm Understanding that his parents were becoming aware of his powers, the Supreme Lord thought that this should not be allowed to happen. Thus he expanded his Yogamāyā, which bewilders his devotees. SB 10.45.1 This will be clear later.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The sun is the sun whether covered by cloud, snow, or eclipse. The covering is not in the sun — it is in the line of sight of the watcher. Bhagavān's awareness is not affected by time or the universe's tides or even by His own self-expansions; only the watcher imagines Him covered by prāṇa and the elements.

    Stories
    Kṛṣṇa untouched in the rāsa-līlā

    Even as Kṛṣṇa multiplies into many forms to dance with each gopī (SB 10.33), He is not divided — He is one, fully present in each, and yet His own awareness is undisturbed by the variety.

    Gauḍīyas read the rāsa-līlā as the operative case of this verse: the Person does not crack; the watcher's eye does.

      ānaka (drum) + dundubhi (kettledrum). The devas sounded drums at his birth, foreknowing that Bhagavān would take him as father. Gauḍīyas treat the epithet as the name's theological resume — Vasudeva's worthiness pre-announced by Svarga.
    • śṛṇvatām — as they listened
      Genitive present participle of √śru. Everyone is listening — the kings, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma. Gauḍīyas note that the verse takes care to record the audience: the sages' instruction is meant to ripen in many hearts, not just Vasudeva's.
    • acyuta-rāmayoḥ — of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma
      Dual genitive. Bhagavān and His first expansion listening to brāhmaṇas instruct on dharma. Gauḍīyas read this as the model of the highest hearers: even Acyuta hears.
    • ābhāṣya — speaking to
      ā + √bhāṣ (to speak). The technical gerund for direct address. The sages do not lecture the field; they speak to Vasudeva, with the field listening.
    [Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:] The sages then spoke again, O King, addressing Vasudeva while all the kings, along with Lord Acyuta and Lord Rāma, listened.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    [Śukadeva Gosvāmī continued:] The sages then spoke again, O King, addressing Vasudeva while all the kings, along with Lord Acyuta and Lord Rāma, listened.
    Commentary

    While the kings, Krsna and Balarama listened the sages spoke to Vasudeva. Genitive case is used instead of locative case here.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    After this, understanding the intentions of Vasudeva and Nārada, to harmonize their intentions, the sages spoke. In verse 41 they resolve Nārada’s statements. They addressed Vasudeva saying, “O crest jewel of success! O most worthy of worship!” The genitive case (sarveṣāṁ śṛṇvatāṁ rājṣāṁ ) is used to express the locative case, since they spoke to instruct the kings. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma listened, since they were present, to approve their words.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    After hearing the glories of Vasudeva, the sages spoke. O king! Śukadeva speaks in bliss because of the glories of Vasudeva. Or he speaks on seeing the beauty of Parīkṣit, who is transformed with prema on hearing about Vasudeva. They spoke while all the kings listened. The instructions were for them. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma also listened in order to affirm the meaning of the sages’ words.

    Important Words
    • viṣṇum — Viṣṇu
      The Lord of all sacrifices, yajña-puruṣa (SB 1.5.32; BG 3.15 yajñārthāt karmaṇaḥ). Gauḍīyas read Viṣṇu as Kṛṣṇa Himself in His sacrifice-receiving aspect — yajña is bhakti's antechamber.
    • sarva-yajña-īśvaram — the Lord of all sacrifices
      sarva (all) + yajña + īśvara. Viṣṇu is the īśvara of every yajña, named or unnamed. Gauḍīyas use this to teach that even nominally polytheistic ritual culminates, properly understood, in service of Viṣṇu.
    • śraddhayā — with faith
      From √śrad-dhā. The ground without which the karma cannot become yajña. Gauḍīyas read śraddhā as the seed of bhakti (CC Madhya 22.62 — śraddhā śabde viśvāsa kahe sudṛḍha niścaya).
    • makhaiḥ — by fire rituals
      Instrumental plural of makha (sacrifice). The technical Vedic word. Gauḍīyas note that the chapter is constructing a bridge from karma-kāṇḍa to bhakti via yajña-as-viṣṇu-pūjā, and these are the bricks.
    [The sages said:] It has been definitely concluded that work is counteracted by further work when one executes Vedic sacrifices as a means of worshiping Viṣṇu, the Lord of all sacrifices, with sincere faith.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    [The sages said:] It has been definitely concluded that work is counteracted by further work when one executes Vedic sacrifices as a means of worshiping Viṣṇu, the Lord of all sacrifices, with sincere faith.
    Commentary

    In this verse the sages reply to Vasudeva’s question about the means of destroying karma by karma. If one does not worship Visnu during the sacrifice, then the karmas are not destroyed.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It is concluded rightly by persons knowing scriptures that actions performed are counteracted by actions being performed. .One should with faith worship Svayam Bhagavān who spreads throughout the universe with his glory by means of all sacrifices. The reason to worship Kṛṣṇa alone in sacrifice is that he gives all results of sacrifices (sarva-yajṣeśvaram) since he is the Lord of all devatās. Without worshipping him even niskāma sacrifices are useless. naiṣkarmyam apy acyuta-bhāva-varjitaṁ na śobhate jṣānam alaṁ niraṣjanam kutaḥ punaḥ śaśvad abhadram īśvare na cārpitaṁ karma yad apy akāraṇam Even the stage of jṣāna without the bondage of karma is not glorious if it is devoid of bhakti to the Supreme Lord. What is the use of having destroyed ignorance? What then to speak of sakāma-karma which causes suffering, both during practice and at the stage perfection, and niṣkāma-karma, when not offered to the Lord? SB 1.5.12 If he is worshipped, then one achieves desired results. However, your son is to be worshipped by another method (not sacrifice).

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Thorn pulls thorn — Karma cancels karma when it is performed as yajña to Viṣṇu, the sarva-yajña-īśvara. Every fire ritual, properly oriented, is a small handle by which the larger boulder of past karma is levered out. The handle works because Viṣṇu is the field of force the handle pries against.

    Stories
    Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya

    In SB 10.74, Yudhiṣṭhira performs the Rājasūya sacrifice — Kṛṣṇa Himself becomes the sarva-yajña-īśvara worshiped first. Gauḍīyas read that scene as the operative example here: yajña is yajña because Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa is its object.

    Important Words
    • upaśamaḥ — pacification, settling
      From upa + √śam (to cease, become quiet). Pacification of the citta — the same the yoga (Patañjali 1.2 — yogaś citta-vṛtti-nirodhaḥ) seeks. Gauḍīyas hold that bhakti-yoga, of which yajña is a limb, accomplishes citta-upaśama by giving the citta a worthy object — Viṣṇu.
    • śāstra-cakṣuṣā — with the eye of scripture
      śāstra + cakṣus (eye). The ṛṣis see by śāstra. Gauḍīyas hold that the Vaiṣṇava sees with three eyes — śāstra, sādhu, and guru — all three saying the same thing about Kṛṣṇa.
    • yogaḥ — means of attaining liberation
      Here yoga = the way. Gauḍīyas note that the verse calls yajña a yoga — placing fire-sacrifice within the yoga genre, with bhakti-yoga as its inner meaning.
    • ātma-mut-āvahaḥ — which brings joy to the heart
      ātma (self, heart) + mud (joy) + āvaha (bringing). Dharma is not killjoy. Gauḍīyas read this as a quiet preview of ānanda-maya — Bhagavān's nature, and the proper telos of every dharma-act.
    Learned authorities who see through the eye of scripture have demonstrated that this is the easiest method of subduing the agitated mind and attaining liberation, and that it is a sacred duty which brings joy to the heart.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Learned authorities who see through the eye of scripture have demonstrated that this is the easiest method of subduing the agitated mind and attaining liberation, and that it is a sacred duty which brings joy to the heart.
    Commentary

    The worship of Visnu is shown to cause peace to the heart (upasama), to be practical (sugama) because it takes shelter of action, to be a method of attaining liberation (yoga), and to give happiness to the mind (atma mudavahah).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The excellence of the method is explained. The method of reduction of karma (ayam) produces intelligence fixed on the Lord (śama) to the highest degree (upa). śamo manniṣṭhatā buddher: śama means fixing the intelligence on the Lord. (SB 11.19.36) This is moreover a process easy to perform. All sacrifices become successful since success is achieved simply by saṅkalpa dedicated to the Lord. It is not difficult to achieve like following the eight parts of yoga. This is the principal dharma since it gives shelter to all dharmas, since this dharma enters all other dharmas. Because it is always filled with the presence of the Lord, it brings joy to the ātmā. It is not like other dharmas filled with lust that makes envy and greed appear in the heart. Therefore this process is revealed by the knowers of scripture, while revealing the meaning of scriptures which are like eyes.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The result is explained. This easy method alone (vai) is encouraged (darśitaḥ) by considering the meaning of scriptures (śāstra-cakṣusā). This method (yogaḥ) is bhakti. It is dharma which is bhakti, since its essence is worship of the Lord. It brings joy to all jīvas (ātma) or when the jīva performs bhakti since it produces a strong relationship with the Lord.

    Analogy

    An overgrown garden, full of weeds and quick growths, needs both the sickle and the careful planting of one true tree. Yajña, when oriented to Viṣṇu, is both — it cuts the agitated mind down and plants something that fruits as joy. The sages call it dharma that brings joy to the heart: not duty-with-clenched-teeth.

    Important Words
    • dvi-jāteḥ — of the twice-born
      dvi (twice) + jāta (born). The brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya — born once of parents, born again of the gāyatrī initiation. Gauḍīyas read the second birth as a precursor to the third — the dīkṣā-janma into Vaiṣṇavism.
    • śuklena — untainted, white
      Pure wealth — honestly earned, not seized. Gauḍīyas treat the cleanliness of wealth as a precondition for yajña: dirty money offered into fire is not pacifying.
    • āpta-vittena — with possessions obtained by just means
      āpta (obtained, attained) + vitta (wealth). Wealth that came rightfully. Gauḍīyas note that the verse spends its weight here — the moral status of the substance is part of the substance.
    • pūruṣaḥ — the Personality of Godhead
      Variant of puruṣa — the Person. Gauḍīyas hold this as the explicit theistic anchor: yajña is offered not to abstract dharma but to a Person, the same Viṣṇu of verse 35.
    This is the most auspicious path for a religious householder of the twice-born orders — to selflessly worship the Personality of Godhead with wealth honestly obtained.
    Purport

    Both Śrīdhara Svāmī and Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī here agree that the ritual karma of Vedic sacrifices is particularly meant for attached householders. Those who are already renounced in Kṛṣṇa consciousness, like Vasudeva himself, need only cultivate their faith in the Lord’s devotees, His Deity form, His name, the remnants of His food and His teachings, as given in Bhagavad-gītā and Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    This is the most auspicious path for a religious householder of the twice-born orders—to selflessly worship the Personality of Godhead with wealth honestly obtained.
    Commentary

    "Purely obtained wealth" means lawfully obtained through the occupations of the three higher castes.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The method is further described. This method is auspicious for the household āśrama, since it pleases the Lord by surrender in the form of offering wealth to the Lord and since the twice- born householder is not qualified for anything accept artha, dharma and kāma. His wealth should be obtained according to his talents in a just manner. Viṣṇu-dharma describes the pure occupation: pratigraheṇa yal labdhaṁ yājyataḥ śiṣyatas tathā // guṇānvitebhyo viprasya śuklaṁ tat trividhaṁ smrṭam yuddhopalabdhaṁ kāraś ca daṇḍaś ca vyavahārataḥ // kṣatriyasya dhanaṁ śuklaṁ trividhaṁ parikīrtitam kṛṣi-vāṇijya-gorakṣāḥ kṛtvā śuklaṁ tathā viśaḥ dvija-śuśrūṣayā labdhaṁ śuklaṁ śūdrasya kīrtitam kramāgataṁ prīti-dāyaṁ prāptaṁ ca saha-bhāryayā aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣām dhanaṁ śukle prakīrtitam śuklena vittena kṛtaṁ puṇyaṁ bahu-phalaṁ bhavet The brāhmaṇa earns wealth purely by donations as gifts, from performing sacrifice and teaching received from persons with good qualities. The kṣatriya earns wealth purely by fighting, receiving taxes, punishment and administering justice. The vaiṣya earns purely by farming, selling and herding cows. The śūdra earns purely by serving the brāhmaṇas, kṣatriya and vaiśyas. Money obtained when getting married, given with affection, and at the proper time, is considered pure for all castes. Performing pious acts with pure wealth produces great results. “If one worships the Lord, he should be worshipped by the main nine types of bhakti or by menial service to the deity and arcana. Is performing sacrifice (which householders perform) a secondary aṅga of bhakti?” This method is for person attached to household life (gṛha-medhinaḥ). This method is taught because the person lacks completely faith, or only to each the common people.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “The direct activities are bhakti with hearing as the main item. Why engage in sacrifices with many secondary parts?” Two verses explain. The auspicious path for attaining bhakti without obstacles (svastyayanaḥ) for the householders of the three upper varṇas is this. One should worship the Lord by money earned by one’s profession in a correct manner. Wealthy persons who are not detached should first offer their wealth in sacrifices.

    Analogy

    For the twice-born householder, śuddha-vitta (untainted wealth) offered into yajña is like fresh ghī into the home fire: the smoke rises straight, the kitchen does not turn black. The same wealth obtained crookedly or offered self-servingly clogs the chimney. The path is straight only because the wealth is.

    Important Words
    • eṣaṇām — desire, craving
      From √iṣ (to desire). The technical Upaniṣadic word (Bṛhad-āraṇyaka 3.5) for the three primal cravings — vitta, putra, loka. Gauḍīyas note that bhakti, when developed, dissolves all three by the substitute desire for Kṛṣṇa.
    • ātma-loka-eṣaṇām — the desire for a higher planet for oneself
      ātma (self) + loka (planet) + eṣaṇā (desire). Even the desire for Svarga must be renounced. Gauḍīyas hold that this verse implicitly contains the entire BG 9.21 teaching — kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśanti — Svarga is impermanent.
    • tapaḥ-vanam — to the forest of austerity
      tapas (austerity) + vana (forest). The vānaprastha destination. Gauḍīyas read this as one of two valid late-life paths — the other being a Vaiṣṇava ashram of bhajana, the second often preferred in Kali-yuga.
    • dhīrāḥ — sober sages
      From √dhṛ (to hold, sustain). The steadied one — the same dhīra of BG 2.13 (dhīras tatra na muhyati). Gauḍīyas hold that dhairya is one of the six limbs of śaraṇāgati (rakṣiṣyatīti viśvāsaḥ rests on dhairya).
    An intelligent person should learn to renounce his desire for wealth by performing sacrifices and acts of charity. He should learn to renounce his desire for wife and children by experiencing family life. And he should learn to renounce his desire for promotion to a higher planet in his next life, O saintly Vasudeva, by studying the effects of time. Self-controlled sages who have thus renounced their attachment to household life go to the forest to perform austerities.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    An intelligent person should learn to renounce his desire for wealth by performing sacrifices and acts of charity. He should learn to renounce his desire for wife and children by experiencing family life. And he should learn to renounce his desire for promotion to a higher planet in his next life, O saintly Vasudeva, by studying the effects of time. Self-controlled sages who have thus renounced their attachment to household life go to the forest to perform austerities.
    Commentary

    One cannot destroy karma without giving up all desires. One can give up all desires by the following process. One should give up the desire for wealth by sacrifice and charity which are the result of the wealth. He then thinks "what is the use of wealth, if it just gets spent in sacrifice and charity?" One should give up the desire for children and enjoyment with wife by enjoying according to the rules of household life. By the experience itself one gives up the desire for it. One should give up the desire for svarga loka by understanding that it is temporary, since the body is subject to death. O Vasudeva (deva), there is proof of such conduct. Giving up their desires in the house, the wise went to the forest.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    By offering various objects to the Lord, by his mercy, one gives up desire for the objects. One gives up desire for wealth by performing sacrifices whose actions expend wealth for the purpose of worship of the Lord. One gives up desire for wife and sons by household life with wife and children meant as worship of the Lord. One should give up desire for selfish reasons or for enjoyment in this life and the next at all opportunities (kālena), looking for opportunities to worship the Lord, using time for the Lord. O Lord (deva)! Or one should give up desires for enjoyment in this life and the next by spending time in worshipping the Lord (deva). The person with discrimination should give up these desires. This means the wealthy householder will not perfect hearing and other devotional process properly by having a disturbed mind. If the attached person suddenly gives up his house without destroying desires for the gṛhasthāśrama, he cannot perfect hearing and meditation on the Lord. He will later give them up.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    By this method the desire for wealth decreases. There is no other way. Examples are given of householders. The discriminating person should act in this way. Otherwise, the wealthy man, with an impure mind, cannot practice bhakti with hearing etc. He should give up his house with it wealth to perfect pure hearing. Thus giving up everything, the intelligent householed (dhīraḥ) goes to the forest. This means that a person who has not become detached, and does not give his desire for wealth, should not renounce.

    Analogy

    The intelligent householder uses each phase of life as a small fire that burns off the corresponding eṣaṇā — yajña and dāna burn off the desire for wealth; family experience burns off the desire for spouse and children; the study of time burns off the desire for heaven. By the time the forest beckons, there is little left to renounce.

    Stories
    Yudhiṣṭhira walking north

    At the end of the Mahābhārata (Mahāprasthānika-parva), Yudhiṣṭhira, having performed his sacrifices and seen his kingdom settled, walks toward the Himalayas with his brothers and Draupadī. The forest is not an escape — it is the after-image of completed eṣaṇā-renunciation.

    Gauḍīyas treat his walk as the operating procedure this verse describes: the sage moves to tapas-vana only after eṣaṇās are quietly burned.

    Important Words
    • ṛṇaiḥ — with debts
      Instrumental plural of ṛṇa (debt) — paired in the verse with tribhiḥ (three). The tri-ṛṇa framework of dharma-śāstra (Manu 6.35). Gauḍīyas note that bhakti, while transcending this framework, does not negate it — Vaiṣṇava householders honor the tri-ṛṇa as part of grhastha-dharma.
    • deva-ṛṣi-pitṝṇām — to the demigods, sages, and forefathers
      Three classes of creditor. Gauḍīyas read service to ṛṣis (svādhyāya, śravaṇa) as the limb closest to bhakti — knowing the sage's teaching is the seed of knowing Kṛṣṇa.
    • yajña-adhyayana-putraiḥ — by sacrifice, study, and children
      Three payment-modes for the three debts. Gauḍīyas note that for a Vaiṣṇava these become viṣṇu-yajña, bhāgavata-svādhyāya, and offering one's children to Kṛṣṇa from infancy.
    • patet — he falls
      Optative of √pat. Falling — not into a metaphor but into actual lower births. Gauḍīyas note that the verse retains the stark eschatology of dharma-śāstra: leaving the debt-stack unpaid has consequences.
    Dear Prabhu, a member of the twice-born classes is born with three kinds of debts — those owed to the demigods, to the sages and to his forefathers. If he leaves his body without first liquidating these debts by performing sacrifice, studying the scriptures and begetting children, he will fall down into a hellish condition.
    Purport

    Concerning the special obligations of a brāhmaṇa, the śruti states, jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇas tribhir ṛṇavāñ jāyate brahmacaryeṇa ṛṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhyaḥ: “Whenever a brāhmaṇa takes birth, three debts are born along with him. He can pay his debt to the sages by celibacy, his debt to the demigods by sacrifice, and his debt to his forefathers by begetting children.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Dear Prabhu, a member of the twice-born classes is born with three kinds of debts—those owed to the demigods, to the sages and to his forefathers. If he leaves his body without first liquidating these debts by performing sacrifice, studying the scriptures and begetting children, he will fall down into a hellish condition.
    Commentary

    The sruti says, "The brahmana is born with debts to these three. By brahmacarya (studying the Vedas) , by sacrifice and by producing children, he is freed from the debts to the rsis, to the devatas and to the pitras." Paying back the debts to them (tani nistirya) one should go to the forest.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    O Lord, capable of relieving us of all debts (prabho)! The incapable person should not be found faulty. One version has pitṛnām. The short ṛ is poetic license. Without liquidating his debts to the devatās (tān or tāni) he encounters great obstracles (patet) in this life and the next. Therefore Manu says vrajati adhaḥ: one should leave the house after this is accomplished. Taking shelter of the Lord is not forbidden at this time. There is no fault in worshipping the Lord even if one has debts. devarṣi-bhūtāpta-nṛṇāṁ pitṝṇāṁ na kiṅkaro nāyam ṛṇī ca rājan sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṁ śaraṇyaṁ gato mukundaṁ parihṛtya kartam O King! One who has given up all varṇāśrama duties and has taken full shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, who offers shelter to all, is not a debtor to or servant of the devatās, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives or Pitṛs. SB 11.5.41

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One must absolve debts to the devatās by sacrifice, just as one absolves debts to sages and pitṛs by study and sons respectively. O Lord, capable of relieving us of all debts (prabho)! The incapable person should not be found faulty. One version has pitṛnām. The short ṛ is poetic license. Without liquidating his debts to the devatās (tān or tāni) he encounters great obstracles (patet) in this life and the next or enters into enjoyment of the house again.

    A twice-born man arrives at human birth carrying three small invoices — owed to demigods (paid by yajña), to sages (paid by svādhyāya), to forefathers (paid by progeny). Leaving the body with the invoices unpaid is exiting the inn without settling the bill: a hell-bound move. The sages name the bookkeeping so Vasudeva can close it cleanly.

    Important Words
    • mahā-mate — O generous one
      mahā (great) + mate (minded). Address of respect. Gauḍīyas note that this is the sages' acknowledgment that Vasudeva already has the qualifications for the next step — they speak to him as one who is ripe.
    • nirṛṇaḥ — without debt
      nir- (without) + ṛṇa (debt). Cleared. Gauḍīyas read this state as the prerequisite for aśaraṇa — only the debt-free man can renounce material shelter without making a mockery of it.
    • aśaraṇaḥ — without material shelter
      a- (not) + śaraṇa (shelter). The state of having no other refuge but Bhagavān. Gauḍīyas read this as a direct preview of śaraṇāgati: 'ananyāś cintayanto mām' (BG 9.22) — non-other refuge is the prayojana of every other limb.
    • unmucya — relieving yourself
      Gerund of ud + √muc (to release upward). To release oneself out of. Gauḍīyas treat this active-voice release as paired with passive grace — one releases by yajña, but final freedom comes from Bhagavān's hand.
    But you, O magnanimous soul, are already free from two of your debts — those to the sages and the forefathers. Now absolve yourself of your debt to the demigods by executing Vedic sacrifices, and in this way free yourself completely of debt and renounce all material shelter.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    But you, O magnanimous soul, are already free from two of your debts—those to the sages and the forefathers. Now absolve yourself of your debt to the demigods by executing Vedic sacrifices, and in this way free yourself completely of debt and renounce all material shelter.
    Commentary

    You are freed from two debts by producing offspring and study. By performing sacrifice you will become free from debt to the devatas . Then renounce the house (asarana bhava).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The word tu indicates Vasudeva in particular. You are certainly (vai) free from debts to Pitṛs and sages. Become completely free (un—mucya) of the three debts and become houseless. Renounce for the sake of Viṣṇu.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The word tu indicates Vasudeva in particular. You are certainly (vai) free from debts to Pitṛs and sages. Become completely free (un—mucya) of the three debts and become houseless. Take shelter (śaraṇaḥ) of Viṣṇu (a). Take shelter of the Lord through hearing etc.

    The sages do Vasudeva's accounting on his behalf: two debts are already cleared (the ṛṣis paid by his lifelong association with them, the forefathers by his sons including Kṛṣṇa Himself). Only the debt to the devas remains — and they prescribe yajña as the closing entry. Once closed, become aśaraṇa — without material shelter — and surrender entirely to Bhagavān.

    Important Words
    • paramayā — supreme
      Instrumental of paramā (supreme). Qualifies bhaktyā — the highest grade of bhakti. Gauḍīyas read paramā-bhakti as approaching prema; the qualification accounts for the result: Bhagavān as son.
    • putratām — the role of son
      From putra + abstract suffix tā. Kṛṣṇa has voluntarily entered into the relation putratām gataḥ — gone-into son-ness. Gauḍīyas treat this as the doctrinal warrant for vātsalya-rasa: the Lord consents to be son because His devotee consents to be father.
    • īśvaram — the supreme controller
      Kṛṣṇa as īśvara of every world (jagatām īśvaram). Gauḍīyas note that the sages do not soften this even as they call Him Vasudeva's son — the two truths are simultaneously asserted: He is the īśvara, He is your son.
    • harim — Lord Kṛṣṇa, Hari
      From √hṛ (to take away, attract). Hari is the One who takes away sins and attracts the heart. Gauḍīyas hold Hari as one of Kṛṣṇa's principal names; the verse uses it deliberately — He who removes (sins) and who attracts (devotees) is the same Person who became Vasudeva's son.
    O Vasudeva, without doubt you must have previously worshiped Lord Hari, the master of all worlds. Both you and your wife must have perfectly worshiped Him with supreme devotion, since He has accepted the role of your son.
    Purport

    Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī paraphrases the sages’ mood as follows: “We have answered you, who questioned us in the manner of ordinary discourse, in the same ordinary way. In truth, however, since you are the eternally liberated father of the Supreme Lord, neither worldly customs nor the injunctions of scripture have any authority over you.” According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī, the very name Vasudeva indicates that Vasudeva manifests brilliantly ( dīvyati ) the superexcellent wealth ( vasu ) of pure devotional service. In the Eleventh Canto Nārada will again meet with Vasudeva and at that time remind him, devarṣi-bhūtāpta-nṛṇāṁ pitṝṇāṁ na kiṅkaro nāyam ṛṇī ca rājan sarvātmanā yaḥ śaraṇaṁ śaraṇyaṁ gato mukundaṁ parihṛtya kartam “O King, one who has given up all material duties and has taken full shelter of the lotus feet of Mukunda, who offers shelter to all, is not indebted to the demigods, great sages, ordinary living beings, relatives, friends, mankind or even his forefathers who have passed away. Since all such classes of living entities are part and parcel of the Supreme Lord, one who has surrendered to the Lord’s service has no need to serve such persons separately.” ( Bhāg. 11.5.41 )

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    O Vasudeva, without doubt you must have previously worshiped Lord Hari, the master of all worlds. Both you and your wife must have perfectly worshiped Him with supreme devotion, since He has accepted the role of your son.
    Commentary

    You have asked a question posing as an ordinary person, and we have answered according to ordinary scriptural rules. But actually since you are the father of the Lord, and a nitya siddha devotee, you do not have to follow the ordinary rules of scripture. But if you think that you are only qualified to following the rules of scripture then listen to what we have said. O Vasudeva, you enjoy ( deva) the treasure (vasu) of bhakti yoga. You have intensely worshipped (pra arcah) the lord with most excellent devotion previously. Therefore, why should you now fall to the lower standard of actions? If it is not so, then our words meaning nothing. The proof is that the Lord himself has appeared as your son. If you want to perform such lower acts out of humility, and taking yourself as a fallen soul, do so just to teach other persons, as the Lord does.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having described the process for persons who have not developed faith in bhakti, now they say that Vasudeva has been most successful from the beginning. O Vasudeva! Vasudeva means he who performs pastimes (deva) with a wealth (vasu) of bhakti for the Lord. They then show how this is true. Certainly you worshipped excellently (pra--arcaḥ) the Lord—as your son, by which you brought him under control. The Lord takes away all suffering (harim), since he is the Lord of all devatās and others (jagatām īśvaram). Therefore you have finished repaying all debts and are to be worshipped by all liberated souls and devotees. With another intention you have also accomplished this. However, this relief from debt is stated according to his imitation of human pastimes, not according to his eternal position. This is indicated by the word Vasudeva itself. Vasudeva refers to the internal śakti of the Lord called śuddha-sattva. It is said in the Fourth Canto: sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ vasudeva-śabditaṁ: śuddha-sattva is called vasudeva. (SB 4.3.23)

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Having described the process for persons who have not developed faith in bhakti, now they say that Vasudeva has been most successful from the beginning. O Vasudeva! sattvaṁ viśuddhaṁ vasudeva-śabditaṁ; the pure antaḥ-karaṇa is called Vasudeva. (SB 4.3.23) Thus Vasudeva has a pure heart, endowed with pure sattva. Or Vasudeva means “he who shines (deva) with a wealth (vasu) of bhakti. That is stated in the verse. Certainly you worshipped excellently (pra--arcaḥ) the Lord—as your son, by which you brought him under control. The Lord takes away all suffering (harim), since he is the Lord of all devatās and others (jagatām īśvaram). Therefore you have finished repaying all debts and are to be worshipped by all liberated souls and devotees.

    Yoga
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The sages turn from accounting to history: a man whose son is Bhagavān must have offered, in some prior life, perfect worship to Hari. Vasudeva's fatherhood is not luck — it is the visible certificate of completed bhakti, hung on the wall of this incarnation.

    Stories
    Vasudeva and Devakī's previous births

    Bhāgavatam 10.3.32–37 narrates that Vasudeva and Devakī were Sutapā and Pṛśni in a previous life, and even earlier Pṛśnigarbha and Kaśyapa — performing austerities to obtain Bhagavān as son. He appeared each time and promised to be born to them again.

    Gauḍīyas read this verse as the sages' diagnostic recognition: prema-bhakti compounded over lifetimes is what produces a parent-of-Bhagavān.

    Important Words
    • mahā-manāḥ — generous, great-minded
      mahā + manas. Generous and large in spirit. Gauḍīyas read this as the standing description of Vasudeva: open-handed in worship, capable of holding Bhagavān as son and as Lord simultaneously.
    • vavre — chose
      Perfect of √vṛ (to choose). Vasudeva chose the very sages who instructed him as ṛtvijas. Gauḍīyas note this as the standard Vedic pattern — the upadeṣṭā becomes the ṛtvij, ensuring continuity between instruction and enactment.
    • mūrdhnā — with his head
      Instrumental of mūrdhan (head). The head touches the ground in praṇāma (mūrdhnā ānamya). Gauḍīyas treat this as daṇḍavat-praṇāma — the highest form of bow — befitting the gratitude of receiving Bhagavān-level instruction.
    • prasādya — gratifying
      Causative gerund of pra + √sad. To please. Gauḍīyas note that gratifying the sage is its own limb of pūjā — the host's joy is itself a sacrament.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After hearing these statements of the sages, generous Vasudeva bowed his head to the ground and, praising them, requested them to become his priests.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: After hearing these statements of the sages, generous Vasudeva bowed his head to the ground and, praising them, requested them to become his priests.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Hearing their words which included his hidden intentions, understanding those words (mahā-manāh) he offered respects.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Hearing their words (from verse 35) he made them his priests. He had a desire to benefit all people by sacrifice, charity and showing the Lord (mahāmanāḥ). Or hearing the words indicating his good fortune because of Kṛṣṇa, he chose them as priests. He thought, “These sages request bhakti. That should be attained from persons like me. On the pretext of a sacrifice I will have them attain Kṛṣṇa’s mercy.” Thus it is later said in verse 49, “Vasudeva’s priests and the officiating members of the assembly, dressed in silk dhotīs and jeweled ornaments, looked effulgent.” He bowed his head completely (ā-natvā), touching the earth and praised them with verses.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Vasudeva, having received the instruction, does not ask follow-up questions or schedule the yajña for next month. He bows his head to the ground, praises the speakers, and chooses them as priests on the spot. The verse's pace is itself the teaching: a clear answer from sādhus is to be enacted, not deliberated.

    Important Words
    • kṣetre — in the holy field
      kṣetra (field). Kurukṣetra — the dharma-kṣetra of BG 1.1. Gauḍīyas read the field as itself a tīrtha; performing yajña there compounds the efficacy of both the rite and the place.
    • ayājayan — they engaged him in executing sacrifices
      Causative of √yaj. The priests do not perform for Vasudeva — they engage Vasudeva in performing. Gauḍīyas note this distinction: the yajamāna is the agent; the ṛtvij is the technician.
    • uttama-kalpakaiḥ — with superexcellent arrangements
      uttama (highest) + kalpa (ritual procedure) + -ka. The technical procedural variants chosen are the best ones. Gauḍīyas note that quality of execution is itself a doctrinal commitment — anything offered to Bhagavān must be the best one has.
    • dharmeṇa — according to religious principles
      Instrumental of dharma. The sages do not innovate; they perform dharma's prescribed forms. Gauḍīyas note this as the conservative wing of the Bhāgavata teaching: spontaneity in rasa, but exactness in vidhi.
    Thus requested by him, O King, the sages engaged the pious Vasudeva in performing fire sacrifices at that holy place of Kurukṣetra according to strict religious principles and with most excellent ritual arrangements.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Thus requested by him, O King, the sages engaged the pious Vasudeva in performing fire sacrifices at that holy place of Kurukṣetra according to strict religious principles and with most excellent ritual arrangements.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The sages engaged Vasudeva correctly, according to the rules of scripture (dharmena), since the brāhmaṇas should direct the kṣatriyas in performance of sacrifice. Or, the brāhmaṇas appointed for the purpose of dharma, engaged Vasudeva, dedicated to bhagavad-dharma (dharmikam), in sacrifice using the chief rules, since they possessed all ability.

    Important Words
    • dīkṣāyām — at the initiation
      From √dīkṣ (to consecrate). Vaiṣṇavas read dīkṣā as the seed-rite of bhajana; here Vasudeva's yajña-dīkṣā is the Vedic precursor to the same notion. Gauḍīyas distinguish karma-dīkṣā from bhakti-dīkṣā but treat both as serious sacraments.
    • puṣkara-srajaḥ — wearing lotus garlands
      puṣkara (lotus) + sraj (garland). The lotus is Viṣṇu's emblem. Gauḍīyas note that lotus-garlands at a yajña are not aesthetic flourish; they are the silent declaration that the yajña is for Viṣṇu.
    • mahiṣyaḥ — queens
      From mahiṣī (chief queen). The verse lists queens with their gifts — registering that yajña, properly done, is performed by householders as a couple-act. Gauḍīyas read patnī-saṁyāja (verse 53) as the codification of this.
    • vastu-pāṇayaḥ — with auspicious items in hand
      vastu (substance, auspicious item) + pāṇi (hand). The hands of the household are full of pūjā-materials. Gauḍīyas treat the hand-fullness of a Vaiṣṇava household as a small marker — what is in the hand reveals what is in the heart.
    When Mahārāja Vasudeva was about to be initiated for the sacrifice, O King, the Vṛṣṇis came to the initiation pavilion after bathing and putting on fine clothes and garlands of lotuses. The other kings also came, elaborately ornamented, as well as all their joyful queens, who wore jeweled lockets around their necks and were also clad in fine garments. The royal wives were anointed with sandalwood paste and carried auspicious items for the worship.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    When Mahārāja Vasudeva was about to be initiated for the sacrifice, O King, the Vṛṣṇis came to the initiation pavilion after bathing and putting on fine clothes and garlands of lotuses. The other kings also came, elaborately ornamented, as well as all their joyful queens, who wore jeweled lockets around their necks and were also clad in fine garments. The royal wives were anointed with sandalwood paste and carried auspicious items for the worship.
    Commentary

    Holding various articles of worship (vastu panayah) in their hands they entered the arena.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The Vṛṣṇis and other kings participated. O king! These kings had good fortune! Addressing the king also indicates Śukadeva’s great joy. Vasudeva’s wives (tad-mahiṣyaḥ) were joyful. The word ca indicates that the Vṛṣṇis and others were similarly joyful. They came close (upa-ājagmuḥ) to the dīkṣa arena.

      Viṣṇu's pāñcajanya. The conch's sound is itself a form of nāma. Gauḍīyas read its appearance in any Vaiṣṇava-context as the Lord announcing His own presence through air.
    • sūta-māgadhāḥ — sūta and māgadha bards
      Two professional reciter-classes. Gauḍīyas note that the recital culture preserved hari-kathā long before written-down texts; the sūta-māgadhas of this verse are the same class as Sūta Gosvāmī of Naimiṣāraṇya.
    • gandharvyaḥ — female Gandharvas
      Celestial singers. Their participation marks the yajña as cosmically attended. Gauḍīyas note that Vaiṣṇava worship draws attendants from every loka — when Bhagavān is the object, the audience is universal.

    Commentary

    Sūṭas, māgadas and women who were singers of the Gandarva species sang.

    Analogy

    The yajña-pavilion sounds like the streets of Vraja during a festival — mṛdaṅgas, paṭahas, conchshells, voices of sūtas and māgadhas, sweet-voiced Gandharvīs singing with their husbands. Vasudeva's sacrifice is staged as a saṅkīrtana before the word existed: the air itself becomes part of the offering.

    Stories
    Caitanya's saṅkīrtana procession

    In Caitanya-caritāmṛta, Mahāprabhu's processions through Navadvīpa and Jagannātha Purī mobilized the same instruments — mṛdaṅga and karatāla in the foreground, conches and drums in the back.

    Gauḍīyas read this verse's audio landscape as the seed of yuga-dharma harināma-saṅkīrtana: the same instruments, eventually re-tuned to the holy name.

    Important Words
    • abhyaṣiñcan — they sprinkled with sacred water
      abhi + √sic (to sprinkle). Abhiṣeka — the consecration rite. Gauḍīyas note that abhiṣeka is one of the core arcana acts; performed on the yajamāna, it consecrates him as ṛtvik-fit.
    • aṣṭā-daśabhiḥ — with eighteen wives
      Eighteen — the number of his wives, the same number as Mahābhārata's parvas and as days of the Kurukṣetra war. Gauḍīyas note Vyāsa's penchant for the number; here it locks Vasudeva into a poetic register of completeness.
    • soma-rājam — the moon-king
      soma (moon) + rāja (king). The standard royal simile in Sanskrit poetry — Vasudeva surrounded by his eighteen wives is like the moon-king encircled by stars. Gauḍīyas note that the simile is reserved for kings worthy of moon-comparison — and Vasudeva, the father of Bhagavān, qualifies.
    • patnībhiḥ — with his wives
      Instrumental plural of patnī. Yajña is performed sa-patnīka — with one's wife. Gauḍīyas read this as the ritual codification of dharma-as-couple: the householder cannot offer alone.
    After Vasudeva’s eyes had been decorated with black cosmetic and his body smeared with fresh butter, the priests initiated him according to scriptural rules by sprinkling him and his eighteen wives with sacred water. Encircled by his wives, he resembled the regal moon encircled by stars.
    Purport

    Devakī was Vasudeva’s principal wife, but she had several co-wives, including her six sisters. This fact is recorded in the Ninth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam: devakaś cograsenaś ca catvāro devakātmajāḥ devavān upadevaś ca sudevo devavardhanaḥ teṣāṁ svasāraḥ saptāsan dhṛtadevādayo nṛpa śāntidevopadevā ca śrīdevā devarakṣitā sahadevā devakī ca vasudeva uvāha tāḥ “Āhuka had two sons, named Devaka and Ugrasena. Devaka had four sons, named Devavān, Upadeva, Sudeva and Devavardhana, and he also had seven daughters, named Śāntidevā, Upadevā, Śrīdevā, Devarakṣitā, Sahadevā, Devakī and Dhṛtadevā. Dhṛtadevā was the eldest. Vasudeva, the father of Kṛṣṇa, married all these sisters.” ( Bhāg. 9.24.21-23 ) Some of Vasudeva’s other wives are mentioned a few verses later: pauravī rohiṇī bhadrā madirā rocanā ilā devakī-pramukhāś cāsan patnya ānakadundubheḥ “Devakī, Pauravī, Rohiṇī, Bhadrā, Madirā, Rocanā, Ilā and others were all wives of Ānakadundubhi [Vasudeva]. Among them all, Devakī was the chief.” ( Bhāg. 9.24.45 )

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    After Vasudeva's eyes had been decorated with black cosmetic and his body smeared with fresh butter, the priests initiated him according to scriptural rules by sprinkling him and his eighteen wives with sacred water. Encircled by his wives, he resembled the regal moon encircled by stars.
    Commentary

    Anointed with anjana on his eyes and smeared with butter on all parts of his body, he appeared like the king of moons (soma rajam)if there were many moons, surrounded by his eighteen wives like stars.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He was like the moon, king of soma. The word “king” is used in remembrance of his participation in the rājasūya sacrifice. The sacrifice was like that rājasūya sacrifice in grandeur. Though there are many somas (moons), among them, one will be the king. He is compared to the king among moons. The other kings are compared to stars. He had twenty-eight wives, but only eighteen participated because twenty-eight was too many. Hari-vaṁśa describes his birth: manuṣya-loke kṛtsne 'pi rūpe nāsti samo bhuvi / yasyāsīt puruṣāgryasya kāntiś candramaso yathā // One could not compare his beauty with that of any human beings on earth. The beauty of the best of men was like the moonlight. Here also he was incomparable.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The wives were the seven daughters of Devaka. There eleven others headed by Rohiṇī. With eighteen wives the scene was very beautiful. The king surrouned by the priests was like the moon surrounded by stars. The word “king” is used to indicate the glory of the sacrifice and its beauty. Hari-vaṁśa describes his birth: manuṣya-loke kṛtsne 'pi rūpe nāsti samo bhuvi / yasyāsīt puruṣāgryasya kāntiś candramaso yathā // One could not compare his beauty with that of any human beings on earth. The beauty of the best of men was like the moonlight.

    Important Words
    • dukūla — silk saris
      Fine silk. The verse lists the householder ornaments — dukūla, valaya, hāra, nūpura, kuṇḍala. Gauḍīyas note that yajña does not require the renunciation of these; it requires the right orientation of them.
    • ajina — deerskin
      Worn by the initiate. The single ascetic element among the householder ornaments. Gauḍīyas read the deerskin not as renunciation but as a marker — the yajamāna is touching the renunciate-register for the duration of the rite.
    • dīkṣitaḥ — having been initiated
      Past participle of √dīkṣ. The state of having entered the yajña. Gauḍīyas note that dīkṣitaḥ is not a permanent identity here — it is the role-state Vasudeva occupies for the rite's duration.
    • vibabhau — he shone brilliantly
      From vi + √bhā (to shine). To shine forth conspicuously. Gauḍīyas treat such verbs in the Bhāgavatam as signals: when something shines, the narrator is pointing out a moment that compresses doctrine into image.
    Vasudeva received initiation along with his wives, who wore silk saris and were adorned with bangles, necklaces, ankle bells and earrings. With his body wrapped in a deerskin, Vasudeva shone splendidly.

    Important Words
    • ṛtvijaḥ — priests
      From ṛtu (season) + √yaj. The priests who officiate by season. Gauḍīyas note that the ṛtvij is a specialist; for Vasudeva's yajña the sages themselves serve as ṛtvijas — an extraordinary upgrading of the office.
    • sadasyāḥ — officiating members of the assembly
      From sadas (assembly hall). The expert witnesses. Gauḍīyas read the sadasyas as a kind of internal review board — yajña is not done in private; it is done before a learned assembly.
    • vṛtra-haṇaḥ — of the killer of Vṛtra (Indra)
      vṛtra (the asura) + han (killer). Indra. The simile names his adhvara (sacrifice) as the benchmark. Gauḍīyas read the simile carefully — even Indra's sacrifice is the comparand, not the original; Vasudeva's yajña stands above it because Bhagavān is its center.
    • virejuḥ — they appeared effulgent
      From vi + √rāj (to shine forth). The priests literally radiated. Gauḍīyas treat radiance in such verses as Bhagavān's prabhā showing through His servants — the priests shine because they are doing what they are made for.
    My dear Mahārāja Parīkṣit, Vasudeva’s priests and the officiating members of the assembly, dressed in silk dhotīs and jeweled ornaments, looked so effulgent that they seemed to be standing in the sacrificial arena of Indra, the killer of Vṛtra.

    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    My dear Mahārāja Parīkṣit, Vasudeva's priests and the officiating members of the assembly, dressed in silk dhotīs and jeweled ornaments, looked so effulgent that they seemed to be standing in the sacrificial arena of Indra, the killer of Vṛtra.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One version has pīta-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ. They were dressed in new cloth similar to the Lord’s. The other version has ratna-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ: they were dressed in cloth with gems hanging at the edges. The simile is used to indicate that just on seeing this, one would become astonished.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    One version has pīta-kauśeya-vāsasaḥ. They were dressed in cloth previously worn by the Lord. By the mercy of Vasudeva they attained perfection of bhakti as they desired. Thus they especially shone. O great king! Śukadeva calls in great joy.

    • jīva-īśau — the two Lords of all living entities
      jīva (living entity) + īśa (Lord), dual. Both Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. Gauḍīyas hold Balarāma as the original Saṅkarṣaṇa, equal in jīva-īśatva and inseparable from Kṛṣṇa in tattva.
    • sva-vibhūtibhiḥ — with the expansions of Their own opulences
      sva (own) + vibhūti (opulence). Sons and wives as personal vibhūtis. Gauḍīyas read this as a precise doctrinal statement: the family of Bhagavān is itself His aiśvarya in embodied form.
    • bandhubhiḥ — with relatives
      From √bandh (to bind). The bound ones — relatives by affection. Gauḍīyas note that bandhu, in Kṛṣṇa's context, carries the connotation of līlā-companion, not merely blood relation.
    • rejatuḥ — the two appeared brilliant
      Dual perfect of √rāj. Both Lords shone. Gauḍīyas note the verb form: two-as-one in the visual register, distinct yet inseparable — the visual instance of acintya-bhedābheda between Kṛṣṇa and His first prakāśa.
    At that time Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, the Lords of all living entities, shone forth with great majesty in the company of Their respective sons, wives and other family members, who were expansions of Their opulences.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    At that time Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa, the Lords of all living entities, shone forth with great majesty in the company of Their respective sons, wives and other family members, who were expansions of Their opulences.
    Commentary

    The lords of all jivas (jivesau), Krsna and Balarama appeared.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    The two lords of the living entities (jīvīśau), like princes or controllers of the population, shone with their intimate expansions -with their cousins (sva-bandhubhiḥ), with their wives, and with their sons who were non-different from themselves in form and qualities (sva-sutaiḥ). They were part of themselves. Or, the two were, in their expansions as Paramātmā, the antaryāmīs of all the jīvas. It is said in the Eleventh canto: kālo māyā-maye jīve jīva ātmani mayy aje: time merges into Saṅkarṣaṇa, and he merges into me. (SB 11.24.27) The Lord is superior to antaryāmī. He is Svayam Bhagavān.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma, equally prominent (ca ca), were surrounded by their intimate friends the cowherds or by relavites, the Yadus and friends, Nanda and others. The wives (dāraiḥ) were naturally theirs eternally. Thus the word sva is not necessary for them. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma were the lords of the jīvas. They were accompanied by their vibhūtis. Or they had the Kaustubha, makara earrings, etc. (sva-vibhūtibhiḥ). The list of persons accompanying the two brothers is in order of increasing proximity.

    Important Words
    • dravya-jñāna-kriyā-īśvaram — the Lord of paraphernalia, mantras, and rituals
      dravya (substance) + jñāna (knowledge, mantra) + kriyā (action, ritual) + īśvara (Lord). Bhagavān is the īśvara of all three dimensions of yajña. Gauḍīyas read this as the technical statement that yajña has no element that is not, ultimately, Kṛṣṇa.
    • prākṛtaiḥ — unmodified, śruti-defined sacrifices
      From prakṛti (original form). The original ritual templates of śruti. Paired with vaikṛtaiḥ — the legitimate adaptations. Gauḍīyas note that Vasudeva performs both grades, the conservative core and the lawful variations.
    • agni-hotra — offering oblations into the sacred fire
      agni (fire) + hotra (offering). The most fundamental fire-rite of the householder. Gauḍīyas note that even now, the Vaiṣṇava brāhmaṇa retains agnihotra; bhakti subsumes it, does not abolish it.
    • īje — he worshiped
      Perfect of √yaj. The internal action of yajña — to worship. Gauḍīyas note that yajña and ārādhana are functionally synonymous: both name the directed offering to a Person.
    Performing various kinds of Vedic sacrifice according to the proper regulations, Vasudeva worshiped the Lord of all sacrificial paraphernalia, mantras and rituals. He executed both primary and secondary sacrifices, offering oblations to the sacred fire and carrying out other aspects of sacrificial worship.
    Purport

    There are numerous kinds of Vedic fire sacrifice, each of which involves several elaborate rituals. The Brāhmaṇa portion of the Vedic śruti specifies the complete step-by-step procedure of only a few prototype sacrifices, such as the Jyotiṣṭoma and Darśa-pūrṇamāsa. These are called the prākṛta, or original, yajñas; the details of other yajñas must be extrapolated from the patterns of these prākṛta injunctions according to the strict rules of the Mīmāṁsā-śāstra. Since other yajñas are thus known by derivation from the prototype sacrifices, they are called vaikṛta, or “changed.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Performing various kinds of Vedic sacrifice according to the proper regulations, Vasudeva worshiped the Lord of all sacrificial paraphernalia, mantras and rituals. He executed both primary and secondary sacrifices, offering oblations to the sacred fire and carrying out other aspects of sacrificial worship.
    Commentary

    Vasudeva worshipped Visnu, the lord of the materials such as oblations, of the mantras (jnana) and of the actions, by primary sacrifices such as jyotisoma, and darsa paurnamsa whose parts are prescribed in detail, and by secondary sacrifices such as the saurya and satra which are modified in form and rule.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He worshipped the Lord according to rules pertaining to sacrifice (anu-yajṣam). The rules are described. He worshipped the Lord of materials, mantras and ritual acts, Bhagavān, since he alone should be worshipped.

    Analogy

    Vasudeva worships the Lord of all sacrificial paraphernalia using the very paraphernalia He is the Lord of — like offering a man flowers from his own garden. The līlā of yajña is that Bhagavān, being everything, consents to be offered with what is already His.

    Important Words
    • dakṣiṇāḥ — gifts of thanks (to the priests)
      Dakṣiṇā is the closing payment that completes the yajña. Gauḍīyas note that yajña without dakṣiṇā is incomplete — the sastra (Manu 11.39) treats stingy yajña as worse than no yajña.
    • yathā-āmnātam — as stipulated in the scriptures
      yathā (according to) + āmnāya (received tradition, śruti). Vasudeva pays according to śruti-prescription, not by improvisation. Gauḍīyas insist that even at the height of generosity, scriptural injunction sets the floor.
    • go-bhū-kanyāḥ — cows, land, and marriageable girls
      go (cow) + bhū (land) + kanyā (girl). The three classical dakṣiṇā items. Gauḍīyas note that the cow heads the list — Bhagavān is gopāla, the cow-protector, and gifts of cows please Him in any context.
    • su-alaṅkṛtebhyaḥ — to those who were richly adorned
      su- + alaṅkṛta (decorated). The priests were already richly adorned. Gauḍīyas read this as a quiet poetic touch: the priests are already glowing; Vasudeva adds to that glow.

    Important Words
    • patnī-saṁyāja — the ritual in which sponsor and wife offer together
      patnī + saṁyāja (joint offering). One of the closing rites of large yajñas. Gauḍīyas note that the ritual codifies what bhakti everywhere asserts — the householder is dharmically a couple, not an individual.
    • avabhṛthyaiḥ — the final ritual baths
      Instrumental plural — from ava (down) + √bhṛ (to bear). The sponsor's closing bath that carries the rite's residual energy into water. Gauḍīyas read avabhṛtha as the sealing seal — yajña ends with water as it began with fire.
    • rāma-hrade — in Lord Paraśurāma's lake
      rāma (Paraśurāma) + hrada (lake). Samanta-pañcaka. Gauḍīyas note that yajña sealed in an avatāra's lake compounds its weight: Bhagavān's water completing Bhagavān's father's offering.
    • yajamāna — the sponsor of the sacrifice
      From √yaj. The one for whom the yajña is performed. Gauḍīyas distinguish the yajamāna (agent) from the ṛtvik (technician) — the agent's interior orientation is what makes the rite efficacious.
    After supervising the patnī-saṁyāja and avabhṛthya rituals, the great brāhmaṇa sages bathed in Lord Paraśurāma’s lake with the sponsor of the sacrifice, Vasudeva, who led them.

    The brahmanas performed a sacrifice called patni samyaja and the actions related to the avabhrtya.

    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    The patnī-saṁyāja and avabhṛthya — the rituals in which the sponsor offers with his wife and then takes the closing bath — are the suturing stitches of the yajña. With these complete, Vasudeva leads the sages in bathing in Lord Paraśurāma's lake: bhagavat-avatāra's water completing the work of yajña on Bhagavān's own field.

    Stories
    Paraśurāma's lakes

    Paraśurāma, after annihilating the kṣatriyas twenty-one times, performed his expiatory rituals at Kurukṣetra and is said to have created five lakes — Samanta-pañcaka — from the blood of the kings.

    Gauḍīyas note that the very water of Vasudeva's avabhṛthya-bath is sanctified by an earlier avatāra's tapas; the geography is layered with Bhagavān's prior interventions.

    Important Words
    • ā-śvabhyaḥ — extending even to the dogs
      ā (extending) + śvan (dog). The verse explicitly names the dog — the unclean animal — as fed. Gauḍīyas read this as the punctum: dharmic completion includes those dharma's normal categories exclude.
    • vandibhyaḥ — to the bards
      From √vand (to praise). The bards praised the yajña; the yajamāna's own ornaments and clothes become their dakṣiṇā. Gauḍīyas note the unusual generosity — typically vandins receive coin, not the host's own garments.
    • annena — with food
      Instrumental of anna (food). Feeding-as-pūjā (annena pūjayat). Gauḍīyas hold prasāda-distribution as one of the dāna-limbs and as a small bhakti-act in itself: the giver, the receiver, and the food are all connected through Bhagavān.
    • varṇān — all classes of people
      Accusative plural of varṇa. Every social class is fed. Gauḍīyas note the verse's deliberate inclusivity — the same scripture that codifies varṇa here universalizes its pūjā at the closing meal.

    Having bathed, Vasudeva, along with his wives, gave to the reciters cloth and ornaments and gave food to all animals from the horses to dogs.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Vasudeva’s queens gave cloth and ornaments to the reciters. Instead of snataḥ alaṅkara sometimes nānālaṅkara is seen. They worshipped the various castes and others down to the dogeaters, by offering food.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    After bathing and decorating themselves they gave away their used ornaments. Women or the queens also gave. Vasudeva fed all four varṇas of people.

    Personal Guidance
    Analogy

    Out of the bath, Vasudeva gives away the very clothes and jewels he wore to the bards, dresses fresh, then feeds everyone — every class of person, down to the dogs. The dharma-act ends where bhakti always wants to start: with the meal that includes even the unincluded.

    Stories
    Prabhupāda's prasāda-distribution

    Across the Bhāgavata tradition, the closing meal of a yajña is meant to include those usually excluded. Prabhupāda institutionalized this in our own time — every ISKCON temple keeps the door open at meal-time.

    Gauḍīyas read this verse, ā-śvabhyaḥ annena pūjayat (he honored even the dogs with food), as the doctrinal seed of that practice.

    Important Words
    • śrī-niketam — the abode of the goddess of fortune (Kṛṣṇa)
      śrī (Lakṣmī) + niketa (abode). One of Kṛṣṇa's titles. Gauḍīyas note that even Lakṣmī takes shelter in Him; the title points to His role as the source of all fortune the guests have just received.
    • pāribarheṇa — with gifts
      pāribarha (royal gift, regalia). The verse names what is given: not stipend but pāribarha — gifts of dignity. Gauḍīyas note that Vaiṣṇava farewell-gifts are not commensurate with value received; they are emblems.
    • śaṁsantaḥ — praising
      Present participle of √śaṁs (to praise, recite). The departing guests recite the glory of the sacrifice. Gauḍīyas read this as a form of yaśo-gānam — bhakti's eighth limb (śrī-viṣṇoḥ śravaṇe parīkṣid, kīrtana being its complement).
    • anujñāpya — taking leave
      Same verb as verse 27. Departure requires permission. Gauḍīyas read this as the standing courtesy of saṅga-dharma: you arrive when invited, you depart when permitted.
    With opulent gifts he honored his relatives, including all their wives and children; the royalty of the Vidarbha, Kosala, Kuru, Kāśī, Kekaya and Sṛñjaya kingdoms; the officiating members of the assembly; and also the priests, witnessing demigods, humans, spirits, forefathers and Cāraṇas. Then, taking permission from Lord Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the goddess of fortune, the various guests departed as they all chanted the glories of Vasudeva’s sacrifice.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    With opulent gifts he honored his relatives, including all their wives and children; the royalty of the Vidarbha, Kosala, Kuru, Kāśī, Kekaya and Sṛṣjaya kingdoms; the officiating members of the assembly; and also the priests, witnessing demigods, humans, spirits, forefathers and Cāraṇas. Then, taking permission from Lord Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of the goddess of fortune, the various guests departed as they all chanted the glories of Vasudeva's sacrifice.
    Commentary

    He worshipped all with affectionate gifts (paribarhena). All of them then left (prayayuh).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He worshiped the Yadus (bandhūn) and the kings of various provinces. He also worshiped all men (nara), Pramathas (bhūta), and devatās. This indicates that all these persons also came to the sacrifice. All were satisfied with the sacrifice by its execution with all limbs and its beauty. Thus they took permission from the Lord and departed.

    Analogy

    The guest-list reads like the rolls of dharma itself — Vidarbha, Kosala, Kuru, Kāśī, Kekaya, Sṛñjaya kings; priests, sadasyas, demigods, men, ghosts, ancestors, Cāraṇas.     Important Words
    • sauhṛda-āklinna-cetasaḥ — whose hearts are melting from feelings of friendship
      sauhṛda (friendship) + ā + √klid (to be wet, melt) + cetas (heart). Hearts liquefied by affection. Gauḍīyas read āklinna-cetas as the bodily mark of prema — the heart literally giving up its shape.
    • viraha-kṛcchreṇa — with the pain of separation
      viraha (separation) + kṛcchra (pain). The Gauḍīya signature category. Gauḍīyas hold viraha as the highest pitch of prema, exemplified by the gopīs at Kurukṣetra (later in this canto, SB 10.82) and by Caitanya's last twelve years.
    • bhagavān vyāsaḥ — the Personality of Godhead Vyāsadeva
      Bhagavān + Vyāsa. Vyāsa addressed as bhagavān — a śakti-āveśa-avatāra. Gauḍīyas note that Vyāsa is called bhagavān because he is the literary embodiment of Bhagavān's own self-disclosure as scripture.
    • pariṣvajya — embracing
      pari + √svaj (to embrace). The closing-embrace before departure. Gauḍīyas note the physical register: the verse measures dharmic-relation in actual embraces, not in abstract sentiment.
    The Yadus were all embraced by their friends, close family members and other relatives, including Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his younger brother, Vidura; Pṛthā and her sons; Bhīṣma; Droṇa; the twins Nakula and Sahadeva; Nārada; and Vedavyāsa, the Personality of Godhead. Their hearts melting with affection, these and the other guests left for their kingdoms, their progress slowed by the pain of separation.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Yadus were all embraced by their friends, close family members and other relatives, including Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his younger brother, Vidura; Pṛthā and her sons; Bhīṣma; Droṇa; the twins Nakula and Sahadeva; Nārada; and Vedavyāsa, the Personality of Godhead. Their hearts melting with affection, these and the other guests left for their kingdoms, their progress slowed by the pain of separation.
    Commentary

    Anuja (younger brother) refers to Vidura.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Friends, relatives and others embraced the Yādavas. Pained by the separation they departed. Others (Duryodhana etc.) however were indifferent.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Vyāsa is called bhagavān because he is an avatāra. Both Nārada and Vyāsa were great gurus and elders. Their hearts melted with affection because they were their friends (bandhūn) and Yadus. Pained by the separation they departed. Others (Duryodhana etc.) however were indifferent.
